Remarks:

  1. The COMPONENT parameter serves for an explicit definition of the component name,
     regardless of the component name defined in the input file. The parameter affects also
     PERMAS input files. It can be reset if necessary setting the name to at least one ’blank’
     character enclosed in single quotes:
     PARAM COMPONENT = ’ ’

  2. The SITUATION parameter serves for an explicit definition of the situation name, regard-
     less of the situation name defined in the input file. For the time being, only the Abaqus
     interface supports this parameter. It can be reset if necessary setting the name to at least
     one ’blank’ character enclosed in single quotes:
     PARAM SITUATION = ’ ’

  3. The CNSTVAR parameter serves for an explicit definition of the constraint variant for the
     input doors. For the time being, only the Abaqus interface supports this parameter.


V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          2-95
    input doors. For the time being, only the Abaqus interface supports this parameter.

6. The RESVAR parameter serves for an explicit definition of the result variant to read in
   results, regardless of possibly existing result variant names in the input file. Currently
   supported doors are Abaqus, MEDINA and PERMAS.

7. The MATPREFIX parameter defines a prefix for the creation of material names from identi-
   fiers. Currently supported doors are MEDINA and NASTRAN. It can be reset if necessary
   setting the name to at least one ’blank’ character enclosed in single quotes:
   PARAM MATPREFIX = ’ ’

8. The ZEROCOORD parameter may be used to correct coordinate tolerances caused by
   numerical errors in mesh generation (e.g. for axisymmetric models). For the time being,
   only the PATRAN interface supports this parameter.

rameter   Type    Value      Explanation

STem                         Calculate up to the generation of system matrices (stiffness,
                             geometrical stiffness).
 DES        I                Number of desired modes for the buckling analysis.
GN        name    BOTH       Compute buckling modes with positive as well as negative
                             load scale factors, sorted by their magnitude.
                 POSITIVE    Compute only modes with positive load scale factors.
                 NEGATIVE    Compute only modes with negative load scale factors.
CTOR       R                 Compute buckling modes up to given load factor limit. The
                             factor is always given as a positive factor, see remark 5 on
                             page 2-107.
                  lsf acl    Optionally, a load factor interval can be defined by a second
                             load factor limit, see remark 6 on page 2-107.

                             one) further vector(s) have converged.

                   NO        Pure buckling analysis without postprocessing data.
HIFT              AUTO       Automatically apply stiffness shifts if they speed up conver-
                             gence.
                   OFF       Do not use shifts in any case.




06               PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                      V 19.00.287
     3-525) within the system variant of the current situation. The geometric stiffness matrix
     is calculated automatically and must not be requested by $ADDMATRIX. The appropriate
     loading state is selected using $ELSTATE LOAD.

  2. System matrix generation is included in the command request. The command may be
     terminated after the system matrix generation using the -SYSTEM- parameter. A contin-
     uation may be done by specifying the -MODES- (and further parameters) later on.

  3. Either the number of modes or a load factor limit must be specified. If both parameters
     are present, the minimum number of modes given by the two parameters are computed.




                                                                                                       EXEC
  4. By default the modes are normalized to the unit value for output purposes. To output the




                                                                                                        UCI
     original (stiffness orthonormalized) modes, set switch MODENORM off (see page 2-25).

  5. The given load scale factor limits are compared with the magnitude of the computed
     factors, e.g. specifying SIGN = NEGATIVE FACTOR = 1.0, 3.0 yields load scale factors
     between −1.0 and −3.0 .

  6. If two load factor limits are given, they define an interval. All modes with load scale factors
     within this interval are computed. The specification of two factors must be combined with
     SIGN = POSITIVE or SIGN = NEGATIVE. Load scale factor intervals are recommended
     for experienced users only.

  7. The shifted algorithm which is enabled by KSHIFT = AUTO may yield much better conver-
     gence. It is therefore recommended to be used especially if many iterations are needed
     to reach convergence.

marks:

1. COMBINE allows to superimpose results referring to loading pattern or time steps by
   application of predefined combination rules.

2. The combination rules are defined in the data input using $COMBINE RESULTS (see
   page 3-1003 ff.) within the result specification bracket.

3. The result combination is performed for the active configuration.

4. If combined results contain any results of non-linear analyses or of analyses with contacts,
   the combined result columns are in general no longer valid results and should be used
   only with extreme caution.

5. If a rule refers to foreign situations, the situations must have been scanned, even if the rule
   is not used by an UCI command. The use of named result variants is therefore strongly
   recommended to avoid unintended reference to a rule.

6. In situ operations (omitting the RESULT option) are only allowed, if the rule refers to
   the current situation only and the analysis is linear. The following points apply to in situ
   operations:

     (a) The item DISPlacement may be overwritten as long as no secondary results have
         been calculated so far. All derived results (e.g. reaction forces, stresses) will then
         be computed using the combined patterns.
     (b) In situ operations on standard results are only possible as long as no derived quan-
         tities have been computed from the primary results. Therefore secondary results
         cannot be combined in situ.
     (c) As an exception, element stresses may be combined without using the RESULT
         parameter. Then nodal point stresses may be computed afterwards containing the
         combined patterns (by using the GENerate command (see page 2-152)).
     (d) For in situ operations, N EW P AT = ON LY can not be applied.
     (e) In situ combination of non-linear results may be enabled by UCI switch NLCOMBINE,
         but see remark 4.

scription:

e nonlinear analysis is realized through a piecewise linear computation. A general nonlinear
ution procedure with line searches is used for the solution. In each loading step, an iteration
 erformed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied.

marks:

1. In nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.

2. Secondary results (including residual and reaction forces) must be computed using the
   GENerate command within the same TASK as the DIRECT NLTEMP command.

3. An additional selection of result steps may be done in the data input of the variant using
   $NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the final solution and the initial values (at TSTART) are
   available.

4. If DIRECT NLTEMP, GENerate and EXPORT are performed in a TASK loop, the current
   results will be generated and exported for each time step contained in the list given by
   $NLRESULTS plus the final solution. Initial values (at TSTART) are not available.

5. XY-results may be extracted from the history information using the XYDATA command of
   the SELECT section.

6. If constant temperature modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of
   the conductivity matrices. Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the singular
   modes is printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extremum
   values as well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a
   local or a global effect has been detected.
   If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
   the constant temperature modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the
   postprocessor. There they may be evaluated in more detail.
   The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command or the setting
   may be included in the default definition file.

7. The setting of a minimum time increment is a break-off criterion for the iteration. If the
   actual time increment is below the given value, the process is terminated. The criterion


26                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         V 19.00.287
     STEPS = LIST is given. In this case the time TEND is equal to the maximum time given
     in the result variant.

  9. The integration parameter γ (GAMMA, SET/SHOW see page 2-37) for the direct integra-
     tion may be modified using the SET command before starting the analysis. However, the
     parameter should be modified only with great care.

 10. Initial conditions may be specified using the $INIVAL definitions in order to continue or to
     refine an analysis.

 11. The definition of a time dependent load $TRANSLOAD is required for the analysis.

     through this parameter, which can lead to larger (or smaller) computational effort.

marks:

1. Unsupported element types are treated as linear (material and geometry). A table of
   supported elements can be found on page 5-16ff. of [um550].

2. In a nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.

3. A combination of PLASTIC/VPLASTIC and NLELASTIC material is not supported, even
   if assigned to different elements. A table of possible material combinations can be found
   on page 5-16ff. of [um550].

4. Secondary results (including residual and reaction forces) must be computed using the
   GENerate command within the same TASK as the DIRECT NLTIME command.

5. Secondary results like stresses and strains are calculated at the Gauss points and as-
   signed (not extrapolated) to the element nodes.

6. A selection of result steps may be done in the data input of the result variant using
   $NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the final solution is available.

7. If DIRECT NLTIME, GENerate and EXPORT are performed in a TASK loop, results will
   only be generated and exported if the current load step is contained in the list given by
   $NLRESULTS.

8. XY-results may be extracted from the history information using the XYDATA command of
   the SELECT section.

9. Initial conditions may be specified using the $INIVAL definitions in order to continue or to
   refine an analysis.

0. The definition of a time dependent load $TRANSLOAD is required for the analysis.

1. Existing non-symmetric material stiffnesses (non-associative plasticity) are always sym-
   metrized.

2. The setting of a minimum time increment TMIN is a break-off criterion for the iteration.
   If the actual time increment is below the given value, the process is terminated. The
   criterion should be applied only with great care, since for a highly nonlinear material
   behaviour, a small time step does not imply convergence.

3. The default value for TEND = 1.0 is overwritten as soon as a result variant using $NLRESULTS
   STEPS = LIST is given. In this case the time TEND is equal to the maximum time given
   in the result variant.

Remarks:

  1. The user may define break points through the definition of the end points of the analy-
     sis. The break points are given through the command alternatives within the PERMAS
     command.

  2. If zero energy modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of the dielec-
     tricity matrices. Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the rigid body modes
     is printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extremum values
     as well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a local
     or a global effect has been detected.
     If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
     the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postproces-
     sor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
     The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66
     ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.

        provided by the user in the current working directory where the PERMAS execution takes
        place. Only an executable script / program will be accepted, not a command in the user’s
        search path.

        mations to the solution script.

     3. Due to the optional result import, the command must be executed in a situation of its own.
        Use separate analysis situations for different executions.

     4. If name is input without quotes, the string is being upcased, otherwise it will remain as
        specified. Please note that the name may be machine dependent.

     5. RESULT specifies a file in PERMAS ASCII (.post) format to be imported after the execu-
        tion has finished. Currently import of results is restricted to $DATA NPUSER.

Remarks:

  1. System matrix generation is included in the command request. The command may be
     terminated after the system matrix generation using the -SYSTEM- parameter. A contin-
     uation may be done by specifying the -MODES- (and further parameters) later on.

  2. One of the parameters -MODES- or -FREQLIM- must be defined in any case. The limit
     which is reached first terminates the analysis. The explicit definition of the number of
     modes is computationally more efficient than the upper frequency limit hence if the num-
     ber of modes is known it is recommended to use the -MODES- option exclusively.

  3. Further parameters for the subspace iteration may be modified using the SET command
     (see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. Those parameters are:

         • ADDVEC, SET/SHOW see page 2-25
         • MAXBOX, SET/SHOW see page 2-39
         • CHEBEXP, SET/SHOW see page 2-34



V 19.00.287                PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         2-145
   original (mobility orthonormalized) modes, set switch MODENORM off (see page 2-25).

5. Ignoration of the compressibility (option NOCOMPR) is only possible if surface wave ele-
   ments are present.

6. Multilevel dynamic reduction is based on a decomposition of the active component in
   subcomponents and the solution of a dynamically (Craig-Bampton) reduced substructure.

7. If external dofs are present on top component level, the Craig-Bampton matrices are
   provided automatically

8. A lower frequency limit is a very specific choice. Please ensure that this is a valid solution
   for your dynamic system behavior. This option is only possible if the shift algorithm is
   being used (see KSHIFT parameter).

9. The vibration analysis is done with a shifted mobility matrix: K ′ = K + α ∗ M . This may
   be used to produce regular modes in case of a system with constant pressure modes,
   i.e. forcing a positive definite instead of a singular mobility matrix. The resulting eigen-
   values/frequencies are shifted back to the original un-shifted problem automatically (the
   eigenmodes are not affected by the shift). However, note that the mobility matrix K ′
   obtained by this shift is not suited for parent situations in further dynamic analyses.

48               PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                     V 19.00.287
  1. The Mobility-Flexibility (MF) Formulation,
     which is obtained by a force formulation of the eigenvalue problem, leading to an inverse
     mass (or mobility) and an inverse stiffness.

  2. The Stiffness-Mass (SM) Formulation,
     which is obtained by replacing the pressure by a suitable kinematic quantity. Hence us-
     ing this method, the decomposition of the compressibility and the mobility matrices is
     performed instead of the decomposition of the corresponding displacement quantities.

For the reader’s convenience some guidelines for deciding whether to use the MF- or the SM-
Formulation shall be summarized subsequently.




                                                                                                      EXEC
                                                                                                       UCI
When the coupled system has neither rigid body modes nor constant pressure modes both
methods are equivalent. If the fluid is incompressible and has no surface waves, the SM-
Formulation might be more efficient. Since the compressibility matrix is zero its Cholesky factor
need not be computed and the operations involving it can be skipped. If, on the contrary, the
mass of the solid structure is so small compared to the mass of the fluid that it can be neglected,
the MF-Formulation is the better method for now the operations involving the Cholesky factor
of the mass matrix can be skipped.

If the coupled system has rigid body modes but no constant pressure modes it is beyond doubt
that the SM-Formulation should be used in order to avoid the problems caused by the singular
coupling term. For the same reasons the MF-Formulation is the appropriate method when
the coupled system has constant pressure modes but no rigid body modes. Remember that
the MF-Formulation must be used if the coupled system has constant pressure modes and a
vanishing compressibility matrix.

If the coupled system has both rigid body modes and constant pressure modes, the singular
coupling term is present as well in the MF-Formulation as in the SM-Formulation. Provided it is
not necessary to use the MF-Formulation because of a zero compressibility matrix that method
should be adopted that allows to approximate the singular coupling term. Should this not be
possible select the MF-Formulation when the number of unknowns of the fluid is small, and the
SM-Formulation if the number of unknowns of the solid structure is small.

The selection of the appropriate method is illustrated by table T2-47.




V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          2-149
          Zero Mass                    no    yes    –     –    no    yes    no


          Appropriate Method           SM    MF    SM    MF    MF    SM     x


                   –   Criterion is not relevant
                   x   MF if additional stiffness can be approximated
                       SM if additional mobility can be approximated

                   Table T2-47: Selection of the Appropriate Method


marks:

1. System matrix and coupling matrix generation is included in the command request.

2. One of the parameters -MODES- or -FREQLIM- must be defined in any case. The limit
   which is reached first terminates the analysis. The explicit definition of the number of
   modes is computationally more efficient than the upper frequency limit hence if the num-
   ber of modes is known it is recommended to use the -MODES- option exclusively.

3. Multilevel dynamic reduction is based on a decomposition of the active component in sub-
   components and the solution of a dynamically (Craig-Bampton) reduced substructure.
   See also default parameters MLDRFAC, DEFAULT see page 2-72 and MLDRSIZE, DE-
   FAULT see page 2-73. Furthermore the UCI switch MLDRFSTA, SET/SHOW see page
   2-40 defines the amplification factor on top component level for the DISP/PRES eigen-
   value analyses.

4. Further parameters for the subspace iteration may be modified using the SET command
   (see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. Those parameters are:

      • ADDVEC, SET/SHOW see page 2-25
      • MAXBOX, SET/SHOW see page 2-39
      • CHEBEXP, SET/SHOW see page 2-34

   However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. Especially parameter
   ADDVEC should only be increased if the frequency limit is used.

5. By default the modes are normalized to the unit value for output purposes. To output the
   original (stiffness orthonormalized) modes, set switch MODENORM off (see page 2-25).

6. The structural mass may be ignored, if it is small compared to the fluid mass. The mass
   matrix is needed if the MF-Formulation is used to analyze a system with rigid body modes.



50                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         V 19.00.287
  8. Mechanical modes are complemented by mode shapes, induced by fluid modes. One
     additional structure mode per fluid mode is generated. Applicable for fluid dominated
     models with very flexible structural behavior. In this case, the MLDRPFAC switch may be
     set explicitly and the MLDRFAC setting might be reduced.

  9. Fluid modes are complemented by mode shapes, induced by structural modes. One addi-
     tional fluid mode per structural mode is generated. Applicable for (nearly incompressible)
     fluids with frequencies above the structural eigenfrequencies. Please check if an increase
     of the fluid frequency limit is more efficient.

 10. The definition of a node set for MLDR is mandatory, if several disconnnected regions exist
     (i.e. separate fluid domains).

1. Primary results must have been computed previously.

2. Generate stresses via the Smooth Patch Recovery method. This method is based on a
   least square fit of a polynomial stress ansatz using stresses at a number of supercon-
   vergent stress points within a patch of elements. Each patch consists of a corner node
   and the connected elements. Hence, SPR stresses can only be determined within ele-
   ments with at least one corner node located in the interior of the mesh. SPR stresses
   are available for the following element families: flange, membrane, solid, shell, solid shell,
   axisymmetric membrane and axisymmetric solid. See section 6.3.1.

   request to get the full history selected by $NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the last state is
   available.

   placements, the application of the element filter will affect these and all derived results.

This is special command to calculate statistics of time history stress results while saving disk
space for the therefor needed stresses/stress resultants. I.e. after a preceeding MODAL
TIMEhistory (or MODAL FSCoupled TIMEhistory) a GENerate MODAL TimeHistory STATistics
can be used to compute modal stresses/resultants and performing a statistical evaluation in the




                                                                                                    EXEC
time domain on-the-fly (without actually storing time domain stresses/resultants) – only the sta-




                                                                                                     UCI
tistical data is saved to disk.

Statistical results are generated for the ESET specified here – completely independent of the
PRIMRES parameter of the MODAL TIMEhistory command (as an alternative the stress/force
statistics can also be calculated in the time domain together with the EVALuation command –
then also relying on the PRIMRES parameter).

For each element, 10 sets of statistical results are calculated as documented for the STATIS-
TICS rule of the EVALuation command, see p. 2-298. The contents of each set depend on
element type and result:

   • MTSIG: stress invariants for shell, solid shell and solid elements
              No.   Shells           Solids
               1    σv , min         σv , min
               2    σv , max         σv , max
               3    σv , upper       σv , mean
               4    σv , lower       σv , mean
               5    σ1 , max         σ1 , max
               6    σ3 , min         σ3 , min
            von Mises and principal stresses

   • MTFORCE: stress resultants for beam and spring elements
     at each element node: forces and moments in the element system
     N, Sx′ , Sy′ , Mx′ , My′ , T
     plus maximum resultant shear force Sm (in total 13 values)

Cutting flux


            GENerate CUTTING FLUX




                                                                                                  EXEC
                                                                                                   UCI
CUTTING FLUX computes the internal heat flow if at least an element set filter is ACTIVE. The
result is given in units of power.

A boundary may be described by defining an active node set in addition, connected to the
elements of the element set. In this case the result represents the flow through the boundary.
The element set defines which side of the boundary and therefore the sign of the flow values.

The sum of the calculated flow values at nodes is written automatically to the result file. The
calculation of the internal heat flow may be invoked several times, previous results will be
overwritten.

       GINERT [    SYSTem       ] [ADDM =   NO   ] [SOLV=           ]

Parameter        Type      Value     Explanation




                                                                                                    EXEC
PRECHECK           -                 Perform a pre-load check (calculate up to the assembly




                                                                                                     UCI
                                     of load matrices). This check of the external loads is not
                                     complete since it does not contain the contribution due to
                                     prescribed displacements and due to inertia forces. Never-
                                     theless, a raw checking is possible, without computing the
                                     system matrices.
SYSTem             -                 Calculate up to the generation of system and mass matri-
                                     ces
DISPlacement       -                 Calculate up to the nodal point displacements and accel-
                                     erations.
ADDM               L       NO        Use only structural mass
                           YES       Take added mass effect of fluid into account (see remark
                                     8)
                           ACC       Accumulate fluid mass to structural mass (see remark 9 on
                                     page 2-194).
SOLV             name    DIRECT      Solution of equations by direct solution method.
                          ITER       Solution of equations by preconditioned conjugate gradi-
                                     ent iteration method (see remark 10 on page 2-194, see
                                     remark 11 on page 2-194).


Description:

The solution calculates the displacements of a free body under static and inertia forces by a
quasi-static solution. As in the standard inertia relief procedure, absolute displacements are
being calculated.

The procedure calculates the inertia forces corresponding to the applied load, i.e. those inertia
forces that generate the opposite reaction forces as the applied loads. The inertia forces are
added to the applied loads and the displacements are calculated under the assumption that the
structure is rigidly restrained at the determinate supports.




V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         2-193
2. The user selects kinematically determinate supports and specifies the related degrees of
   freedom as $RIGMODE (see page 3-377 ff.).

3. The static loads are applied as usual. Additional, nonlinear (displacement dependent
   loads) may be introduced with the $LCMATRIX (see page 3-835 ff.) statement.

4. The user may define break points through the definition of the end points of the analy-
   sis. The break points are given through the command alternatives within the PERMAS
   command.

5. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined.

6. The complete loads including the inertia forces (but not the displacement dependent
   loads) are stored in book UBLIR.

7. If rigid body modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of the system
   and load matrices. Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the rigid body
   modes is printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extremum
   values as well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a
   local or a global effect has been detected.
   If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
   the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postproces-
   sor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
   The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66
   ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.

8. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and in-
   terface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is taken
   into account only for the solution of the eigenvalue problem and the subsequent effective
   mass computation, the structural mass matrix remains unchanged.

9. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and in-
   terface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is added to
   the structural mass and is valid for all subsequent computations using the same system
   matrices.

0. The selection of an iterative solution method is especially of interest, if the resulting sys-
   tem matrix is nonsymmetric (due to loading contribution).

1. An important setting to save disc space is the GINERTFLEX = OFF setup.

TSTART             R                  Starting time for analysis, only applicable for contact
                                      analysis with load history. If omitted the minimum time

                                      remark 6.

                                      with load history. If omitted the maximum time given by
                                      $NLRESULTS (or $NLLOAD) is used, see remark 6.


Description:




                                                                                                     EXEC
                                                                                                      UCI
The solution calculates the displacements of a free body under static and inertia forces by a
quasi-static solution. This procedure is known as ’inertia relief’.

The procedure calculates the inertia forces corresponding to the applied load, i.e. those inertia
forces that generate the opposite reaction forces as the applied loads. The inertia forces are
added to the applied loads and the displacements are calculated such that they do not contain
any rigid body motions.

Remarks:

  1. The model must contain rigid body modes, which may either be determined automatically
     or explicitly be specified by the user with $RIGMODE.
     The deprecated way of specification by $EXTERNAL is no longer possible.

  2. The static loads are applied as usual, but a loading variant is expected to be present also
     for all subcomponents, since the analysis creates additional loads.

  3. The user may define break points through the definition of the end points of the analy-
     sis. The break points are given through the command alternatives within the PERMAS
     command.

  4. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined.

  5. The static loads are applied as usual. Additional displacement dependent loads may be
     introduced with the $LCMATRIX (see page 3-835 ff.) statement.

  6. If a load history (i.e. $NLLOAD) is given the calculation is performed in the quasi-time
     domain from TSTART to TEND, with the default values:
           TSTART = min time from $NLLOAD and/or $NLRESULTS,
           TEND = max. time from $NLRESULTS if existing, from $NLLOAD otherwise.
     Note that the UCI parameter TSTART and TEND can only limit the time range of the
     pre-defined load history from $NLLOAD and $NLRESULTS, respectively, i.e. it is not
     possible to add new additional time steps by this option.



V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          2-199
   Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the unspecified rigid body modes is
   printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extreme values as
   well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a local or a
   global effect has been detected.
   If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
   the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postproces-
   sor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
   The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66
   ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.

9. If REFERENCE is set to CENTER, the displacements are determined such that the center
   of gravity does not move. For partially supported structures, the center of the moving part
   is kept in place. No $RIGMODE definition is required for REFERENCE = CENTER.
   If REFERENCE is set to RIGMODE, the displacements are determined such that the
   degrees of freedom specified by $RIGMODE are not moving. If no $RIGMODE is given,
   the computation aborts with an error.
   The deformation only differs by rigid body motions for both settings of REFERENCE.
   Therefore secondary results such as stresses are identical.

0. The number of rigid body modes NOFRBM must only be specified if they shall be detected
   automatically and the number is not six.
   If the rigid body modes are defined with $RIGMODE, the parameter NOFRBM is not
   needed.

1. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and in-
   terface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is taken
   into account only for the solution of the inertia relief problem, the structural mass matrix
   remains unchanged.

2. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and in-
   terface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is added to
   the structural mass and is valid for all subsequent computations using the same system
   matrices.

3. All failure functions defined in the reliability situation are processed, each leading to a

   analysis will be active.

3. The xy-data are prepared for the currently active node set, which should be activated
   within the task mode before specifying the modal frequency command. They contain the


10                 PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                        V 19.00.287
     to extract results in a local coordinate system.

  5. If PRIMRES=REDUCED has been selected, the nodal point results are computed for
     all nodes, referred by the active node set or the active element set. Secondary results
     for elements are possible, if an element set has been activated previously. Primary and
     secondary results in subcomponents are not available. Residuals and reaction forces
     may be calculated only in single components.
     At least one set (node or element set) must be active when applying the -REDUCED-
     command option.

  6. The excitation frequencies are defined in the result variant ($FREQUENCY (see page
     3-1046 ff.), see section 3.2.7).




                                                                                                     EXEC
                                                                                                      UCI
  7. The definition of a frequency dependent load ($FREQLOAD (see page 3-816 ff.)) is
     required for the analysis.

  8. The iterative solver is available for symmetric and non-symmetric problems with constant
     damping and stiffness matrices. Exception: Diagonal frequency-dependent Control-6
     elements are supported. The iterative solver is especially fast for many excitation fre-
     quencies and a limited number of load cases per excitation frequency. The accuracy can
     be controlled with the ACCuracy option, the default value is 4.0, leading to a residual error
     of 10−4 = 0.01%.

  9. The solution scheme is recommended for a large modal basis and only few discrete vis-
     cous damping elements. It is applicable if:

        • The viscous damping matrix is constant, symmetric and positive-semidefinite. Ex-
          ception: Frequency-dependent symmetric Control-6 elements are supported.
        • There are no additional (symmetric or quadratic) stiffness contributions.
        • Elemental structural damping is not frequency dependent.
        • There is no viscous damping in subcomponents (for MLDR CONF = TOP: All viscous
          damping elements must be in the top component).
        • Control elements may have frequency dependent stiffness, structural- or viscous
          damping.

     The inversion is performed using the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury (SMW) formulation.

 10. The system option allows to prepare condensation matrices of a component with external
     dofs for a subsequent export. Condensed loads are only prepared for the system option.

 11. If several dynamic load cases shall be analyzed in the same job, the use of an assembly
     situation should be considered for performance reasons. System and result variant must
     be identical, only the loading variant may differ. See $SITUATION and example DRA3V2.

   are prepared: eigenfrequencies (RSFRQ), damping coefficients (RSDMP) and equivalent

2. A free vibration analysis must have been performed previously to this command. The
   subsequent modal complex analysis may be grouped within the same task as the vibration
   analysis in order to scan the whole computational task.

3. After the modal complex eigenvalue calculation, the situation used for the free vibration
   analysis will be active.

4. If PRIMRES=REDUCED has been selected, the nodal point results are computed for
   all nodes, referred by the active node set or the active element set. Secondary results
   for elements are possible, if an element set has been activated previously. Primary and
   secondary results in subcomponents are not available. Residuals and reaction forces
   may be calculated only in single components.

   command option.

   elapsed time.

   complementary to the optional frequency limit.

7. If no eigenmode fulfils the given selection (e.g. only unstable modes selected but there is
   no unstable mode), then the first eigenmode is kept.

8. For the generation of XY-data for a Campbell diagram always the complete set of com-
   plex eigenfrequencies is used, frequency limit and backtransformation filters UNSTABLE
   and POSREL are ignored. So the numbering of XY-data sets and the selected set of
   eigenvectors may be different.

9. For RFREQ=EIGFREQ the computation of equivalent viscous damping is performed with
   the eigenfrequency of each mode, instead of a constant reference frequency.

Remarks:

  1. A free vibration analysis must have been performed previously to this command. The
     subsequent modal time history may be grouped within the same task as the vibration
     analysis in order to scan the whole computational task.




                                                                                                      EXEC
  2. After the modal time history analysis, the situation used for the free vibration analysis will




                                                                                                       UCI
     be active.

  3. The integration parameters α , β and δ for the integration rules may be modified using the
     SET command (see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. However, those parameters
     should be modified only with great care. If δ is changed, the Hilber Hughes Taylor method
     is used as integration method instead of the newmark family of methods. In this case α
     and β are modified internally in order to get an unconditional stable algorithm.

  4. When using nonlinear elements, the algorithm is no longer unconditional stable, so the
     time step has to be selected carefully.

  5. The xy-data are prepared for the currently active node set, which should be activated
     within the task mode before specifying the modal time history command.

  6. The xy-data are always related to the component system. The command TRANSFORM
     (see page 2-325 ff.) in conjunction with XYDATA (see page 2-327 ff.) can be used in order
     to extract results in a local coordinate system.

  7. Initial conditions may be specified using the $INIVAL definitions (see page 3-832) in order
     to continue or to refine an analysis.

  8. If PRIMRES=REDUCED has been selected, the nodal point results are computed for
     all nodes, referred by the active node set or the active element set. Secondary results
     for elements are possible, if an element set has been activated previously. Primary and
     secondary results in subcomponents are not available. Residuals and reaction forces
     may be calculated only in single components.
     At least one set (node or element set) must be active when applying the -REDUCED-
     command option.

  9. PRIMRES=NONE can drastically reduce disk space in case the MODAL TIMEhistory is
     just used as a predecessor for a succeeding GENerate MODAL TIMEhistory STATistics
     or GENerateFATIGUE analysis only and no actual time domain results are needed (i.e.
     if MODAL TIMEhistory is used to just generate the modal time participation factors).




V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           2-239
  ADDMODE definitions) shall be filtered out.

2. DELTA = -0.05 means smooth algorithmic damping. An increase of the absolute value of
   the parameter increases also the algorithmic damping.

3. Structural (respectively material) damping is not defined for the time domain and must
   therefore be converted into an equivalent viscous damping. The reference frequency for
   the conversion is set by system variant $PARAMETER (see page 3-546 ff.) RFREQC and
   RFREQE.

4. MODAL TIMEHISTORY supports the following non-linear elements: NLSTIFF, NLSTIFFR,
   NLDAMP, NLDAMPR, CONTROL3, CONTROL6 and HYST3. In this case the desired ac-
   curacy may be given with the ACCURACY parameter.

5. The system option allows to prepare condensation matrices of a component with external
   dofs for a subsequent export. Condensed loads are only prepared for the system option.

is performed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied. The material law is integrated on

scription:

e nonlinear analysis is realized through a piecewise linear computation. A general nonlinear
ution procedure with line searches is used for the solution. In each loading step, an iteration
 erformed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied. The material law is integrated on
ment level at the Gauss points by various techniques.

marks:

1. Unsupported element types are treated as linear (material and geometry). This will affect
   results especially for NLGEOM = YES! A table of supported elements may be found on
   page 5-16ff. of [um550].

2. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined. Please refer
   to Example CA1 of [um550] on page 4-103 ff.

3. In a nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.

4. A combination of PLASTIC/VPLASTIC and NLELASTIC material is not supported, even
   if assigned to different elements. A table of possible material combinations can be found
   on page 5-16ff. of [um550].

5. Secondary results (including residual and reaction forces) must be computed using the
   GENERATE (see page 2-152 ff.) command within the same TASK as the NLMATERIAL
   command.

6. By default, secondary results like stresses and strains are calculated at the Gauss points
   and assigned (not extrapolated) to the element nodes. Use DEFAULT SET EXSLEN and
   EXSNEN to request extrapolation.

7. A selection of result steps may be done in the data input of the result variant using
   $NLRESULTS (see page 3-1053 ff.). Otherwise only the final solution is available.

8. If NLMATERIAL, GENerate and EXPORT are performed in a TASK loop, results will
   only be generated and exported if the current load step is contained in the list given
   by $NLRESULTS.

9. XY-results may be extracted from the history information using the XYDATA command of
   the SELECT section.




48                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         V 19.00.287
     mation may indicate whether a local or a global effect has been detected.
     If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
     the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postproces-
     sor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
     The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66
     ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.

 11. Existing non-symmetric material stiffnesses (non-associative plasticity) are always sym-
     metrized.

 12. The setting of a minimum time increment is a break-off criterion for the iteration. If the




                                                                                                    EXEC
     actual time increment is below the given value, the process is terminated. The criterion




                                                                                                     UCI
     should be applied only with great care, since for a highly nonlinear material behavior, a
     small time step does not imply convergence.

 13. When a combined geometrical and material nonlinear analysis is performed the geometric
     nonlinear part is treated with the co-rotational theory. No coordinate updates are done.

 14. The Thomas acceleration can be used solely for plastic and viscoplastic models (MAT =
     PLASTIC/VPLASTIC) in a geometric linear analysis (NLGEOM = NO).
     For models containing HEXE8 elements it is important to replace them by HEXFO8 el-
     ements, since the Thomas method is not suitable for elements with internal degrees of
     freedom.

 15. Without further specifications, the default value is TEND = 1.0.
     With $NLLOAD and $NLRESULTS given in the data input, the default value for TEND is
     the maximum time given in the result variant by $NLRESULTS.
     If the TEND parameter is specified, it defines the final time of the analysis independent of
     the settings in the data input.

 16. In the predictor step, convergence is always checked with the force criterion, the selection
     is only considered in the corrector step. The actual values are printed to the log file.

  1. In nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.

     local or a global effect has been detected.

     the constant temperature modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the

scription:

e optimization problem posed in the data input is solved by the selected optimization method.

mination criteria can be set by the parameters TOLOBJ, CSTVIOL and TOLDV, see re-
rks 3 and 14. The maximum number of iterations is controlled by the LOOPS parameter of
  TASK command. The maximum step size for design variable changes may be manually
 trolled by using $DSVMLIM.

e optimization is performed in a situation of its own, referring to analysis situations which are
be included in the optimization process. See the CONNECTED option of $SITUATION.

Remarks:

  1. Contact analysis may be performed in STATIC, INERTIA RELIEF and NLMATERIAL ana-
     lyses. In case of NLMATERIAL, or if design constraints CAGAPS, CAPRES or CAREAC
     (see $DCONSTRAINT on page 3-898 ff.) are used in the optimization, only optimization
     methods working with the option DSMETHOD = NONE may be used.

  2. Property values ($GEODAT) dependent on design variables may be prepared as elemen-
     tal post-processing result by GENerate EPRES, see example OP15. The updated coor-
     dinates of a shape optimization are available as result by ITEM COORdinate CHANGE




V 19.00.287                 PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                       2-255
   CSTVIOL). If set, for convergence it is required that the maximum relative change of the
   design variables in the last iteration is below the given value. An application are problems
   which have no feasible solution.

4. Switching between DSMETHOD = DIRECT and ADJOINT is only possible for STATIC,
   INERTIA RELIEF, MODAL FREQuency and TEMPerature analyses. The selection of the
   most efficient method is also dependent on the available disk space. If a large number of
   design variables is defined, the direct method may be limited by the fact, that each design
   variable will cause a full right hand side. In this case, the adjoint variable method might
   help (at computing time costs for a large number of constraints).

5. Methods of the “AOS” module may be used also with DSMETHOD = NONE. For gradient
   based methods, derivatives will then be calculated by difference quotient, leading to an
   extra analysis for each design variable.

6. Optimization including design elements of type DBEAD, DFREE and DTOPO (see
   $DELEMENT) is not possible with DSMETHOD = NONE.

7. The ACP method uses a more conservative constraint approximation than e.g. the con-
   vex approximation scheme and is recommended for highly nonlinear behavior. This may
   be caused by manufacturing restrictions or also by constraints like frequency response
   quantities. It is also quite well suited for very large optimization problems, since it has
   out-of-core capabilities.

8. The Global Domain Centering (GDC) approach looks for a sphere with maximum diame-
   ter inside the feasible region, not for a single optimal solution point. Use DSMETHOD =
   NONE for this option.

9. The Locally improved Dividing Rectangle (LDR) algorithm is a derivative free method
   to detect a global extremum. It is suited for a small number of design variables. Use
   DSMETHOD = NONE to save computation time. Requires the “AOS” module. Exhausting
   the maximal number of loops is the only termination criterion for this method.

0. The MultiStart (MS) method uses local optimizers with several starting points. It requires
   the “AOS” module. This method exhausts the maximal number of loops. Termination
   of the underlying local optimizers can be controlled by the parameters TOLOBJ and
   CSTVIOL. The following specific settings may be changed by UCI command DEFAULT
   SET:

      • OPTMSUBMETH
      • OPTMSEED

1. The Optimality Criteria (OC) method is a derivative free method for nodal point stresses.
   The usage of DFREE design elements is mandatory, see example OP19.
   Besides stress as constraint or objective, further design constraints may be defined if
   analytical derivatives are available.



56                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          V 19.00.287
 13. The Wedge-constrained Linear programming (WLIN) method is a derivative free method,
     use DSMETHOD = NONE to save computation time. Requires the “AOS” module.

 14. The termination criteria for the methods of the “AOS” module are different from the default
     convergence criteria:

        • The global methods have no other criterion than reaching the maximal number of
          loops.
        • The convergence criterion is not applied, if the algorithm is in some special phase,
          e.g. initial sampling or construction of finite differences. The WLIN method has a
          sampling phase during the first (designvariables + 1) loops.




                                                                                                     EXEC
        • All the local methods are Trust Region methods, i.e., they adaptively control the




                                                                                                      UCI
          step size. These methods are designed to guarantee convergence to some point
          which may be a solution of the optimization problem or not. The latter case is called
          unsuccessful convergence.
        • Successful convergence is reached when
          |f (best) − f (k) | < otol · |f (best) | and
           (k)
          cj - c̄j < cviol · |c̄j |, j = 1 . . . m.
          Note that the current objective function value is compared to the objective value of
          the best known point and not to the value of the last point (which is the default when
          a non-“AOS” method is selected).
        • Unsuccessful convergence is reached whenever
              – the relative step size is smaller than the parameter TOLDV
              – and the successful convergence criterion is not satisfied
              – and the algorithm is not in some special phase, e.g. initial sampling or construc-
                tion of finite differences.
          The default value for “AOS” methods is TOLDV=1.0E-5.

 15. The following default switches control the advanced optimization solvers (AOS):

        • OPTSUBTOL
        • OPTPENAL0
        • OPTPENAL1
        • OPTRUSTSIZ0 and OPTRUSTSIZ1

marks:

1. The reliability based optimization analysis is done in an own situation, referring to analy-
   ses which are to be included in the analysis process.

2. The maximum number of iterations is controlled by the LOOPS parameter of the TASK
   (see page 2-55 ff.) command.

3. Only one failure function is possible in reliability based optimization analysis.

4. The number of iterations in the inexact line-search algorithm is limited either by fulfillment
   of the convergence criterion or by reaching the limiting iteration number.

5. The exact line search algorithm is entered only if the iteration limit was reached in the
   inexact line-search algorithm.

6. The iteration is terminated if the β values of two subsequent iterations differ by less than
   ǫ. The allowed range is [0.5x10−4 ≤ ǫ ≤ 0.5].

marks:

1. System matrix generation is included in the command request. The command may be
   terminated after the system matrix generation using the -SYSTEM- parameter. A contin-
   uation may be done by specifying the -MODES- (and further parameters) later on.

2. One of the parameters -MODES- or -FREQLIM- must be defined in any case. The limit
   which is reached first terminates the analysis. The explicit definition of the number of
   modes is computationally more efficient than the upper frequency limit hence if the num-
   ber of modes is known it is recommended to use the -MODES- option exclusively.



64                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                      V 19.00.287
        • MAXBOX
        • CHEBEXP

     However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. Especially parameter
     ADDVEC should only be increased if the frequency limit is used.

  4. By default the modes are normalized to the unit value for output purposes. To output
     the original (permeability orthonormalized) modes, set switch MODENORM off (see page
     2-25).

  5. Further parameters are active in case of the iterative solver, namely:




                                                                                                   EXEC
        • MAXITS




                                                                                                    UCI
        • TOLITS
        • MBLKITS
        • THETA
        • ZETA
        • RBMITS
        • MAXNIT

     They may be modified using the SET command (see page 2-25) before starting the anal-
     ysis.

  6. The iterative solver is restricted to diagonal conductivity matrices, hence only the diago-
     nal mass approach is possible and no MPC-conditions or substructuring models may be
     treated for the time being.

  7. The usage of the iterative solution method may be advantageous especially in case of
     good conditioned structures. The saving of disk storage is especially for larger models
     considerably, since only an incomplete decomposition of the stiffness matrix is performed.

  8. Rigid body modes are treated different by using the iterative solver. The direct solver
     separates the rigid body modes (as far as detected) from elastic modes of the structure,
     whereas the iterative method computes the rigid body modes like elastic modes.

marks:

1. System matrix generation is included in the command request. The command may be
   terminated after the system matrix generation using the -SYSTEM- parameter. A contin-
   uation may be done by specifying the -MODES- (and further parameters) later on.

2. One of the parameters -MODES- or -FREQLIM- must be defined in any case. The limit
   which is reached first terminates the analysis. The explicit definition of the number of
   modes is computationally more efficient than the upper frequency limit hence if the num-
   ber of modes is known it is recommended to use the -MODES- option exclusively. For
   multilevel dynamic reduction (MLDR), however, the parameter FREQLIM must be speci-
   fied in any case.

3. The accuracy given by the -ACCURACY- parameter is only valid for the first eigenvalue.
   The relative accuracy decreases for higher frequencies until a minimum accuracy is
   reached, which can be set by the default switch MINEVACC, DEFAULT see page 2-72.

4. Further parameters for the subspace iteration may be modified using the SET command
   before starting the analysis:

       • ADDVEC
       • MAXBOX
       • CHEBEXP

   However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. Especially parameter
   ADDVEC should only be increased if the frequency limit is used.



78                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                       V 19.00.287
     modes. In order to have consistent results in the output, switch MODENORM must be set
     OFF.

  7. Effective masses are computed for supported vibrations in order to have a measure for
     the completeness of the modal model.

  8. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and in-
     terface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is taken
     into account only for the solution of the eigenvalue problem and the subsequent effective
     mass computation, the structural mass matrix remains unchanged.

  9. The vibration analysis is done with a shifted stiffness matrix: K ′ = K + α ∗ M . This




                                                                                                      EXEC
     may be used to produce regular modes in case of a system with rigid body motions,




                                                                                                       UCI
     i.e. forcing a positive definite instead of a singular stiffness matrix. The resulting eigen-
     values/frequencies are shifted back to the original un-shifted problem automatically (the
     eigenmodes are not affected by the shift). However, note that the stiffness matrix K ′
     obtained by this shift is not suited for parent situations in further dynamic analyses.

 10. Multilevel dynamic reduction (MLDR) is based on an automatic decomposition of the ac-
     tive component into subcomponents and the solution of a dynamically (Craig-Bampton)
     reduced substructure. The frequency limit for the condensation of subcomponents is
     calculated as FREQLIM×MLDRBFAC respectively FREQLIM×MLDRFAC and the basic
     component size is controlled by default switch MLDRSIZE. For a reduction of the interface
     see default switch SUBGRED.

 11. CONF = ORIG performs a back-transformation of the eigenvectors to the original compo-
     nent. Subsequent modal response analyses will be performed on the original component.
     CONF = TOP performs no back-transformation. Subsequent modal response analyses
     will be performed on the top component of the MLDR tree. This is the most efficient
     option, if response results are required at a few locations only.

 12. If external DOFs are present on top component level, the Craig-Bampton matrices are
     provided automatically

 13. A lower frequency limit is a very specific choice. Please ensure that this is a valid solution
     for your dynamic system behavior. This option is only possible if the shift algorithm is
     being used (see KSHIFT parameter).

 14. If some eigenmodes seem to be rigid body modes, a rigid body mode update may be
     done. Then the lowest eigenmodes are moved to the rigid body modes. See also the UCI
     switches RBMCHECK and RBMUP_EDIST/RBMUP_RDIST.

                                                                     EXTENDED




                                                                                              EXEC
                                                                                               UCI
Parameter        Type       Explanation

TYPE                        There are two independent types of weight analyses:
              ELEMENTAL     The elemental weight analysis computes mass, center of grav-
                            ity and inertia tensor for each element. These are summed up
                            to obtain the total mass etc. of the model. Therefore only con-
                            tributions of elements are taken into account (see remark 2 for
                            details).
              STRUCTURAL    The structural weight analysis is based on structural matrices
                            similar to the mass matrix. Therefore all contributions to the
                            mass are considered (see remark 5).
SETS                        Select an element set for elemental weight analysis:
                ACTIVE      Use active element set (remark 3). If no active set is present,
                            the default set containing all elements of the appropriate de-
                            gree of freedom type is used, e. g. ELEMDISP (see also
                            $ELEMENT).
                 ALL        In a loop over all (appropriate) element sets, mass and inertia
                            information is printed for each set (see remark 4).
DOFTYPE                     Select degree of freedom type for elemental weight analysis:
                DISP        Evaluate the weight of structural elements.
                PRES        Evaluate the weight of fluid elements.
OUTPUT                      Select how much information is printed for structural weight
                            analysis:
              STANDARD      Standard output only in the top component of the active config-
                            uration.
              EXTENDED      Extended output for all components (see remark 6 for details).




V 19.00.287               PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                      2-281
2. The elemental weight analysis is based on a direct summation of element contributions.
   Thus a direct matrix input is not taken into account and, for assembled components, only
   the mass introduced by the elements of the actual component is taken into account.
   It always uses a lumped mass approach (diagonal mass) – regardless of the
   $PARAMETER MASS setting.

3. The elemental weight analysis may be performed also for a part of the structure by acti-
   vating an element set previous to the weight analysis (see ACTIVE).

4. If SETS = ALL is chosen for the elemental weight analysis, all sets of one degree of
   freedom type are evaluated for weight analysis consecutively. If a set name ends with
   a different degree of freedom identifier as the currently active one, it is skipped (e. g.,
   default extension is DISP, set name ends with TEMP).

5. The structural weight analysis is applicable at each component level, but is restricted to
   DOFTYPE = DISP. As it is based on matrices, it is computational more expensive than
   the elemental weight analysis and no element sets can be chosen. All contributions from
   substructures, nonstructural mass ($NSTRMASS) and added fluid mass are taken into
   account.
   The structural weight analysis is based on consistent mass matrices, unless diagonal
   mass is selected explicitly with the system block $PARAMETER MASS.

6. For the extended output option, condensed mass matrix BMMC and principal inertias
   are printed in addition. Mass properties are output for each component of the active
   configuration instead for the top component only.
   Furthermore, the mass properties may be related to an arbitrary reference node by the
   system block $PARAMETER REFNODE.

7. Please store the condensed and directional mass (BMMC, BMMCT, BMXRC and BMXRH)
   for matrix models to obtain a correct structural weight output.
   If the above books are not available, the structural weight analysis uses the condensed
   mass matrix SMM as an approximation, which is incomplete if not all DOFs are external.
   Please refer to example DEVX1V1 on page 8-15 ff. of [um550].

8. For models using dry condensation of fluid, the fluid mass is contained in the mass cal-
   culation once the solution step is performed. Please refer to example DEVX2V1 on page
   8-34 ff. of [um550].

9. System mass matrix generation is included in the command request for both types.

               RESULT = name          SETS = [ nset [, [sr ] [, [si ] [, [fun r ] [, [fun i ] ] ] ] ] ]20
                                                                                                       1




                                                                                                                    SELECT
Description:




                                                                                                                      UCI
The command derives new results R by modification of existing results X in a region of the
model defined by a node set. A function f (X) is applied to the original result values X. The
outcome is then multiplied by a scaling function s(c), which is a function of the column value
(time, frequency, load pattern id, etc.). The equation is as follows:


                                           R = s(c) ∗ f (X)

where:
 R       Is the derived result
 s(c)    Is the scaling factor, determined by the evaluation of a function s at the
         current column value c (time, frequency, load pattern id)
 f (X)   Is the function applied to the original result values X
 X       Is the original result

In case of complex arithmetic, a pair of functions must be given. The application of function fun r
to the complex result X gives the real part, which is subsequently multiplied with the scaling
function sr . The same holds for the functions fun i and si , which form the imaginary part of the
derived result R (see remark 2 and 3):


                                      Re(R) = sr (c) ∗ fr (X)
                                      Im(R) = si (c) ∗ fi (X)



Parameter          Type       Value       Explanation

DISPlacement                              Transform displacement item
VELOcity                                  Transform velocity item
ACCEleration                              Transform acceleration item
PRESsure                                  Transform pressure item



V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                                          2-285
                                        tion application (optional)
SULT             name                   (Pre-) Name (max. 7 char.) of (not yet existing) result book,
                                        mandatory (see remark 5 and 6).
TS                                      Allows to specify up to 20 tupels consisting of:
                 name       nset        Nodal point set and
                 I>0      s∗ / fun ∗    Label (integer, name or text string) of the applied functions
                name/text               (see remark 2).


marks:

1. The APPLY command is restricted to nodal point results. The value function f (X) is
   applied individually to each component (i.e. DOF) of the original result X.

2. The first (sr ) and third (fun r ) function labels in the list create the real part of the new result
   R, the second (si ) and fourth (fun i ) create the imaginary part. In case of real arithmetic,
   only the labels sr and fun r may be given, si and fun i must be left blank.

3. In case of complex arithmetic, fun r and fun i should in general be functions of two vari-
   ables. Otherwise only Re(X) will be used as input to the function.

4. The modification rule for the data is an overwrite rule, which keeps all initial data un-
   changed except the regions that are modified. The user is responsible for the definition of
   unique sets. If a node is part of several sets, only the last modification rule will be applied.

5. In case of complex arithmetic the resulting book names are built from the name pattern
   according to the following rules:
    name      Denotes the amplitude data
    nameF Stores the phase data
    nameR Is the real part
    nameI     Is the imaginary part of the result

6. The standard books associated with PERMAS items may not be changed in situ. User
   books with user defined labels may be used in several subsequent APPLY commands,
   allowing to split operations.

7. Within a task, the function application is performed for the active component only.

8. PERMAS functions are defined in the data input using e.g. $FUNCTION TABLE (see
   page 3-1151 ff.)

rameter     Type      Value     Explanation

UATION     name                 Name of an existing situation to be cleared.
                                All corresponding results are deleted.
ADING               MODULE      Clear contents of the loading module of active situation.
                                The loading module contains load matrices derived from the

marks:

   objects of the result module of the situation are deleted. Furthermore, the situation is
   prepared for a new computation. Nevertheless, the situation definition remains valid.
   This means that the variants which build the situation are not changeable. But if several
   analysis types may be performed within one situation (e.g. eigenvalue analysis and linear
   static analysis) the situation may be used for a new computation.

4. Caution : All results must have been evaluated before clearing the situation.

5. The usage within task loops is not possible. Subsequent computations should be per-
   formed in separate tasks.

marks:

Parameter      Type   Explanation

MODES           I     No. of modes requested for export.


Description:




                                                                                               SELECT
The command may be applied after a VIBration ANalysis command and modifies mass and




                                                                                                 UCI
stiffness matrices to shift eigenfrequencies according to the input given by a $EFREQMOD
data block. The modified data objects are intended to be exported to Excite.

Remarks:

  1. The EFREQMOD command expects that in the vibration analysis all elastic eigenmodes
     are calculated.

  2. The eigenmodes requested by parameter MODES are orthonormalized with respect to
     modified mass matrix; the sequence of modes, however, is kept. So the corresponding
     eigenfrequencies may be no longer in ascending order.

  3. The EFREQMOD command must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness
     and mass matrices have to be reassembled internally before modification. Otherwise, the
     FREQLIM parameter of the VIBration ANalysis command must be used.

Remarks:

  1. The MAXMINSCALAR rule is applied to all columns j (e.g. time, frequency or load pat-
     tern) of each data row i of the input item. The SCALAR is build from the tensor according
     to the given evaluation option (PRINCIPAL, SX, SY or SZ). For the principal option the
     largest principal value is used.
     This option produces a result book with 4 columns which are defined as follows.

       Column            formula           description
                     ⌢
              1:     x i = maxj aij        Maximum of all SCALAR values in row i
                     ⌣
              2:     x i = minj aij        Minimum of all SCALAR values in row i
                               ⌢      ⌣
              3: Rangexi = x i − x i       Range of SCALAR values in row i
                          ⌢      ⌣
              4:   x̄i = ( x i + x i )/2   Mean value of SCALAR values in row i


  2. The MAXMINTENSOR rule produces a result book, containing for each nodal point n, the
     following 5 stress tensors σmax (n), σmin (n), σamp (n), σmean (n), and σrng (n). The tensors
     are computed by the following procedure:
     Denote by ρ(A) the spectral radius of a matrix A, i.e.

                                   ρ(A) := max{|λ| : λ is eigenvalue of A}.

     Then ρ(σ) is the principal stress with the largest absolute value. Furthermore let N de-
     note the number of nodal points in the mesh, L the number of (selected) result columns
     (loading patterns, time steps) and σ(n, l) the nodal point stress tensor of nodal point n for



V 19.00.287                        PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                    2-299
 and search at each node n the pair (i∗ , j ∗ ) for which ρ is maximal. This is the pair with
 the largest stress difference. If there is no unique maximum, (i∗ , j ∗ ) will be the first pair
 found having the maximum value.
 The procedure yields the two tensors σ(n, i∗ ) and σ(n, j ∗ ). The tensor with the largest
 principal stress (respecting the sign) is denoted by σmax (n), the remaining one is denoted
 by σmin (n).
 Using these two tensors, we define
 the maximum amplitude stress tensor

                              σamp (n) := (σmax (n) − σmin (n))/2,

 the mean stress tensor

                              σmean (n) := (σmax (n) + σmin (n))/2,

 and the range stress tensor

                                 σrng (n) := σmax (n) − σmin (n).

Description:

Perform the generation of a surface/line mesh (hull) based on the given dimension of the se-
lected elements.

Optionally, a smoothed geometry may be created based on the discrete hull. Moreover, a
polygon reduction may be performed, based on a triangularization of the surface mesh. This
reduction is not applied to lines and leads to a representation that is intended to be used as a
basis for a re-creation of the geometry.


Parameter        Type       Value        Explanation

EFRATIO                                  Element filling ratio (topology)
AUTO                                     Automatic selection of minimum filling ratio (see remark
                                         1).
MINFILL           R     0 < f rat ≤ 1.   Explicit definition of minimum filling ratio for the selec-
                                         tion process.
ESET             name                    Direct selection of elements for the hull generation pro-
                                         cess.
NEWCOOR                                  Use updated coordinates instead of initial ones (see re-
                                         mark 4).
BOOK             name                    Name of an existing input book to be used for extraction
                                         (optional)
SMOOTH                                   Create a smoothed hull geometry.
SMITER             I         50          Number of smoothing iterations.
LEVEL              I         5           Smoothing level



V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                            2-301
L             R           1.0        Geometry tolerance for coarsening (see also TDEF pa-
                                     rameter).
EF          name         REL         The tolerance criterion is relative to the average mesh
                                     size.
                        ABS          Absolute tolerance given by the TOL parameter.
                        POLY         Specify the desired reduction ratio of polygons as given
                                     by the TOL parameter.
XANGLE        R           5.         Limit for the maximum surface normal angle (in de-
                                     grees) deviation before and after a contraction step.


marks:

1. The automatic selection of contributing elements for topology optimization is performed
   based on the selection of the mean value of the filling ratio minus 2.0 times the standard
   deviation. At least one third of the mean value is being chosen.

2. For multiple invocation of the command, the previous result will be destroyed.

3. For polygon reduction, always the stronger criterion (given by TOL and MAXANGLE) is
   applied.

4. An additional smoothing step for a shape optimized structure may be performed by ap-
   plying the smoothing option.

5. In VisPER, a hull generation with interactive modification of the parameters is possible,
   see VisPER User’s Manual, Visualization dialog. The final hull may then be exported also
   in STL format.

6. Export of the hull is possible by ITEM TOPO SMOOTH.

ample:

export of smoothed hull after topology optimization
SELECT
   ACTivate SITuation = topo
   HGEN EFRATIO SMOOTH
EXPORT
   ITEM CLEAR
   ITEM TOPO SMOOTH
   GO FILE = hull
