Parameter        Type         Value     Explanation




                                                                                                    UCI
CRITERION       name                    Specify the ply failure criterion.
                           HOFFMAN      This global stress criterion considers differences in
                                        tensile and compressive failure.
                            TSAI_WU     This global stress criterion is described by a general
                                        tensor polynomial approach including an additional
                                        interaction parameter F ∗ . It considers differences in
                                        tensile and compressive failure.
                             USER       A user defined criterion is applied on the input book
                                        (see $PLYFAILPAR).
PARAM          pfpname                  Name of parameter data set for ply failure criterion
                                        evaluation (see $PLYFAILPAR).
BOOK             name                   Name of (non-standard) input book to be used.
RESULT         name[1-8]                Unique name of evaluation result to be used for sub-
                                        sequent operations (max. 8 characters).


Remarks:

  1. The definition expects element stresses for laminate elements related to the laminate ma-
     terial system, created by the UCI-command GENerate ELement STRESS. The element
     stress format is described in the element atlas (see chapter 4 ff.).

  2. The evaluation process is performed for the active set of laminate elements of the active
     component. The set must be explicitly activated beforehand by the command ACTIVE.

  3. The input parameters for a user defined ply failure criterion must be specified by the
     DAT-Definition $PLYFAILPAR, see remark 10 on page 3-1059.

14   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)   V 19.00.287
                      [MACLIM = lim]
                      [DISTOL = tol]
                      [INCR = inc]
                      [ADDNODES = nset]




Parameter            Type         Value     Explanation




                                                                                                     SELECT
LOOPS               I >0           80       Maximum number of iterations to fulfill MAC criterion.
MACLIM                             0.1      Maximum acceptable degradation of off-diagonal




                                                                                                       UCI
               0.0 < lim < 1.0
                                            MAC values (see remark 5).
DISTOL             R > 0.0         1.0      Distance tolerance to find neighbors of “nominal” node
                                            set (see remark 7).
INCR            0.0 < inc < 1.0    0.01     Increment to reduce amplitude border (see remark 6).
ADDNODES             name                   Name of a node set that shall be part of the final node
                                            set in any case.


Description:
The command tries to find an appropriate set of nodes that are representative for the given
modal basis (X r ). The MAC criterion is applied to the reduced nodal basis
                                                   (X tr X r )2
                              M AC =
                                          diag(X tr X r )diag(X tr X r )
in order to check the mode separation. If the desired maximum off-diagonal value is not reached
within the given number of iterations, the best state is selected automatically. Finally, two node
sets are prepared for further processing:

  1. A minimum set, that may be used to restrict the modal displacements (see EXPORT,
     PARAM). For this minimum set, a coarsening is being performed around the nodes with
     extremum values to clearly identify the extremum.
  2. An extended set (driven by DISTOL parameter) to get additional “neighbor” nodes, that
     may be of interest for measurement positions. A corresponding element set may be
     used to output a partial model. This extended set is always named as PRETEST. A
     corresponding element set with the same name is also prepared in order to be able to
     output a partial model (see remark to ITEM PART on page 2-390).

Of course, also all intermediate node sets are indicated and may be inspected manually. For
them, the EXPORT, CURRENT command may be used to restrict the displacement results,
after knowing the setname.


V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          2-315
2. A partial model may be used for the operation using the NSET option of the ACTIVE
   command.

3. The mode normalization must be switched on by SET MODENORM = ON.

4. The function works only for modal solutions in the currently active component.

5. The termination criterion is the sum of the MACLIM value and the highest off-diagonal
   value of the full MAC matrix of the (partial) model. Note that even in the full MAC matrix
   the off diagonal values will not be totally zero, because the eigenvectors are normalized
   to X t KX = I and not to X t X = I.

6. The increment is used as a relative multiplier (scaled with the loop number) to select
   additional extremum nodes within each level:
   Rlim = Rmax − IN CR ∗ LOOP .

7. The distance is given in model units and has to be adapted by the user.

ase refer to example DEV6A of [um550].

Remarks:




                                                                                                            UCI
  1. The book is expected to be freedom oriented (internally partitioned). For nodal point
     partitioned books see APPLY (see page 2-285 ff.) command.

  2. If only 1 coefficient is given, all dofs of the matrix are scaled uniformly with this coefficient.
     Otherwise, the coefficients must be given for each dof direction separately.

  3. The global scaling of a matrix is a dangerous action. The presence of MPCs may lead to
     undesirable results since the final matrix is a condensed one (only guiding dofs present).
     The user is responsible to check the validity of this scaling approach.

Example:

 SCALE BOOK = SMM.DISP         COEF = 1.125
 SCALE BOOK = SKM.DISP         COEF = 2.,1.,1.,1.,1.,1.

Remarks:




                                                                                                     UCI
  1. The command transforms results from the frequency domain into the time domain. Op-
     tionally, the superposition of a static load pattern is possible.

  2. A frequency response calculation must have been performed before. Each invocation
     will create a new result (that might overwrite an already existing one). Either one single
     frequency or one or more of its harmonics can be considered.

  3. The DOFTYPE parameter is currently only needed in case of reaction forces for a coupled
     computation.

  4. Within a task, the transformation is performed for the active configuration. Outside of the
     task, only the currently active component is handled.

  5. The total time equals one period of the lowest frequency. If not specified, the number of
     time steps is chosen such, that one period of the highest frequency is subdivided in 24
     steps.

  6. By default, the labels are built by adding SST to the standard labels of the corresponding
     item, leading to following labels:


                                 Item                    Name

                                 DISPlacement            USRSST

Remarks:

  1. The availability of sumload items is the same as for the GENERATE command. If not




                                                                                                     SELECT
     already present, the secondary results will be generated within the command. Primary
     quantities like loads are being created by a preceding command.




                                                                                                       UCI
  2. If NSET is specified, the node set must be an ordered set, that corresponds with its
     dimension to the leading set bin. It contains the reference nodes for the load summary. If
     omitted, the summary is related to the component system. If RSYS is given, the reference
     direction is taken from the reference coordinate system.
  3. RSYS defines the reference system for transformation. Can be supplied to NODE, NSET
     or COG reference node. If neither NODE, NSET nor COG is specified, the reference
     node is taken from RSYS (P 0) definition.
  4. For the summation of nodal force quantities only NSETBIN is applicable.
  5. For the summation of element energies or weights only ESETBIN is applicable.
  6. For CUTTING FORCE, ESETBIN and NSETBIN are possible (as for the original CUT-
     TING FORCE command option of the GENerate command).
  7. For the calculation of cutting forces at a wetted surface in a fluid-structure coupled analy-
     sis, the fluid structure interface elements must be part of the element sets. Otherwise the
     contribution of the fluid pressure will be missing.
  8. The DOFTYPE option is mandatory for the computation of reaction forces. PRES is
     currently not supported for cutting forces.
  9. Displacement dependent loads, described by $LCMATRIX are currently only supported
     by the INERTIA RELIEF command, that must precede the SUMLOAD command to create
     the loads.
 10. The computation of rigid body accelerations is based on structural weight analysis, that
     has to be performed in advance.
 11. The summation of relative quantities (i.e. densities) makes sense only, if the elements
     are about the same size.
 12. Item LOAD is only supported for DOFTYPE = DISP.

scription:

default xy curves are extracted such, that the abscissa value is given by the column (i.e.
ding case, time, etc.) and the ordinate values are the result data. For each selected node or
ment (s. remark 1) and data component a curve will be created.
 a special case it is possible to create xy data for nodal point results with a coordinate
ection as abscissa by selecting the COOR option, see remark 6. For each result column (i.e.
ding case, time, etc.) and data component a curve will be extracted.

marks:

1. The extraction process is performed for the active node/element set of the active com-
   ponent. The set must be explicitly activated beforehand by the command ACTIVE (see
   page 2-61 ff.).

2. For each item a default name for the xy-data pre-name exists (see section export (EXPORT
   (see page 2-363 ff.)) for details.

3. The xy-data are not overwritten. If data for the same ITEM are extracted repeatedly, the
   RESULT option must be used to create a new set of curves.


30                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                       V 19.00.287
     results. For complex results, a pair of real / imaginary values may be extracted instead. If
     the BOOK option is used, the label of the amplitude book must be specified in combination
     with TYPE=COMPLEX.

  6. If a coordinate direction is selected by option COOR, the abscissa values correspond to
     the coordinates of the selected nodes, sorted along the selected axis in ascending order.
     Each result column and data component will lead to one curve. A selection of desired
     columns (by SELECT CURRENT (see page 2-291 ff.)) is recommended. The option is
     applicable for nodal point data only.

  7. RSYS=sysid selects a reference coordinate system for the COOR option. The meaning
     of the coordinate values depends on the chosen reference system. The output of angles




                                                                                                    SELECT
     is performed in degrees.




                                                                                                      UCI
  8. In case of RSYS=ROTB, nodal point results will be output in the ROTB system. This
     renders a preceding TRANSform TO ROTB unnecessary.
     If combined with option COOR, coordinates are sorted with respect to the component
     system.

  9. For complex arithmetics, the user may define a reference node, defining a reference
     phase angle (for each selected dof). The amplitude value is then projected with the phase
     difference of the selected node (and dof) to the reference node (/dof)
     (R = A ∗ cos(φref − φ)).
     I.e. the resulting real part of the quantity refers to the same state.

 10. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single dcomp
     selections or range selections. Up to 10 dcomp numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may
     be specified.
     DCOMP = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects dcomps 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.

 11. Result items which cannot be selected directly may be extracted by selecting a similar
     item and then using the BOOK option with the appropriate label. See Appendix F for the
     data object labels.

CTIVE NSET = SET_N1

 Sort nodes in set ’result’ by global x-coordinate and extract dof 2
 (LPAT 1 and 2 only)
URRENT LPAT = 1,2
CTIVE NSET = result
YDATA DISP COOR=X DCOMP=2

 Extract forces of spring elements at 2nd element node
 and create a set of curves according to element type

AT           ∗                    Reset loading pattern selection.
           I[,/I]                 Define subranges of loading pattern to be printed. De-
                                  fault are all loading pattern. The parameter refers to
                                  all results which contain loading case dependent data
                                  (see remark 2).
          LAST                    Selects the last column of the matrix.
EQUENCY     ∗                     Reset frequency value selection.
          R[,/R]                  Define subranges of frequencies to be printed. Appli-
                                  cable to all frequency dependent data (see remark 2).
          LAST                    Selects the last frequency value of the matrix.
ME          ∗                     Reset timestep selection.
          R[,/R]                  Define subranges of time steps to be printed. Applica-
                                  ble to all time dependent data (see remark 2).
          LAST                    Selects the last timestep of the matrix.
LUMNS        ∗                    Reset column selection.
           I[,/I]                 Define subranges of columns to be printed. Default
                                  are all columns of the data object. The parameter is
                                  applied if no more specific selection is available (e.g.
                                  LPAT, TIME or FREQUENCY) (see remark 2).
          LAST                    Selects the last column of the matrix.
OMP        I[,I]                  Define a subrange of data components to be printed.
                                  This allows to restrict the output of all books which are
                                  nodal point partitioned (not applicable for element and
                                  xy data). E.g. the output of displacements may be
                                  restricted to translational freedoms (data components
                                  1 to 3) for: DCOMP = 1,3 .
RMONIC       ∗                    Reset harmonic selection.
             I                    Define one harmonic to be printed. This is only used
                                  for harmonic balance results.
MTYP      name         RELative   Define a relative limit see remark 3.
                       ABSolute   Define an absolute limit.
OVE         R                     Define an upper limit of values. (Absolute) Values be-
                                  yond that limit will not be printed. The meaning of the
                                  option refers to the -LIMTYP- option. If a relative limit
                                  is chosen, the value defines a percentage.
LOW         R                     Define the lower limit of values. (Absolute) Values be-
                                  low that limit are not printed. The meaning of the input
                                  refers to the limit type. See remark 4.
ET        name            ∗       Reset element set to default name (dependent on de-
                                  gree of freedom type).

NSET             name           ∗         Reset node set to default name (dependent on degree
                                          of freedom type).
                                -         Choose an existing node set to restrict the print of
                                          data. This option overrules the ACTIVE setting.
HISTORY          name                     Optimization history / task loop data print settings, can
                                          be set by the default switch HISTORY, DEFAULT see
                                          page 2-70, see remark 6 on page 2-337:
                            LOOP          Output of (history) data for task loops.
                          ITERATION       Output of (history) data for iterations, i.e. optimization
                                          cycles.




                                                                                                       PRINT
                         PROGRESS         Output of (history) data for progress steps, i.e. an im-




                                                                                                        UCI
                                          proved design state.
                           RESULTS        Output of (history) data for results of subproblems, i.e.
                                          a converged solution for multistart or Pareto.


Remarks:

  1. The definition of output settings is valid only for the currently active situation and com-
     ponent. If a change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be
     done again since the valid selection range usually has changed.

  2. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single se-
     lections or range selections. Up to 10 numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may be
     specified.
     COLUMNS = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects columns 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.
     TIME = 1.0,3.0 / 5.0 / 8.0,10.0 selects time ranges 1.0 to 3.0, 5.0 to 5.0 and 8.0 to 10.0 .

  3. Relative limit is supported for modal participation factor print only.

  4. To print also lines which contain only zero values, use CURRENT BELOW = 0.0.

  5. Self expanding field formats are also possible instead of fixed values. See appendix H for
     further information.

  6. To have a valid filtering, please perform any print after the optimization solution took place.
     The filter works in two ways:

        • For a task loop that doesn’t match the criterion, the print is completely switched off
          (only for the current active task).
        • For a matching task loop, the selected items are printed and the (optimization) xy
          data are being filtered according to the criterion.

  1. The requested data object must exist

  2. The regular print request is not valid for complex arithmetics. Books with datatype com-
     plex may be dumped. Usually, the decomposition in amplitude/phase and real/imaginary
     part exists and may be printed.

Remarks:

  1. The command performs selection and output of the result in tabular form to the result file.

  2. The output of node and element results is performed for the currently active node set,
     respectively element set, only. The CURRENT NSET / ESET command overrules any
     settings by the command ACTIVE. The filter works only for standard scalar, vector and
     tensor results, but not for e.g. XYDATA.

  3. With option BOOK, a non-standard result may be printed, e.g. created with the RESULT
     option of a preceding UCI command. If the result is of complex arithmetic type and should
     be printed as complex result, the option COMPLEX must be used instead. Here the name
     of the amplitude book must be specified.

  4. For standard labels of the PERMAS result items, please refer to chapter 7.2.5.

ameter       Explanation

F            No output of summary data.
L            Output of all summary data, (STATISTIC is used, not FSTATISTIC).
TATISTIC     Additional output of statistical data, the data is interpreted as a function y = f (x) .
NMAX         Output of extrema.
OW           Show current settings.
ATISTIC      Additional output of statistical data.


marks:

1. The summary selection is valid until it is redefined or the section is exited.

2. The summary data settings are independent from the settings of the data object contents
   (see CONTents command).

3. Available for nodal point and element scalar results only.

4. If the x-interval between data pairs (xi , yi ) is of importance for the calculation of statistical
   data, the data points can be interpreted as a piecewise linear function y = f (x) (option
   FSTATISTIC). This is for example useful to interpret results, where the x-values are not
   equidistant.

5. For XY data output statistical values for data rows are printed, if SUMMary is set to
   (F)STATISTIC.

                                  gree of freedom type)
                          -       Choose an existing element set to restrict the export
                                  of data

                                  of freedom type)
                          -       Choose an existing node set to restrict the export of
                                  data

             I                    Define one harmonic to be printed. This is only used
                                  for harmonic balance results.

                       ABSolute   Define an absolute limit

HISTORY         name                    Optimization history/task loop data output settings,
                                        can be set by the default switch HISTORY, DEFAULT
                                        see page 2-70, see remark 8 on page 2-369.
                           LOOP         Output of (history) data for task loops
                         ITERATION      Output of (history) data for iterations, i.e. optimization
                                        cycles
                        PROGRESS        Output of (history) data for progress steps, i.e. an im-

                          RESULTS       Output of (history) data for results of subproblems, i.e.

                                                                                                       UCI
Remarks:

  1. The definition of output settings is valid only for the currently active situation and com-
     ponent. If a change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be
     done again since the valid selection range usually has changed.
  2. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single se-
     lections or range selections. Up to 10 numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may be
     specified.
     COLUMNS = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects columns 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.
     TIME = 1.,3. / 5. / 8.,10. selects time ranges 1. to 3., 5. to 5. and 8. to 10.
  3. The settings are valid for all selected items, therefore CURRENT must precede the ITEM
     command.
  4. A reduction of output data may be defined in row (node/element) and column (e.g. LPAT,
     TIME) direction using the appropriate settings.
  5. Corner node results are only supported for MEDINA. MEDINA is not able to handle fully
     quadratic elements (e.g. HEXE27, PENTA18, QUAM9) with corner node results properly.
  6. The BELOW filter is currently only applicable for modal participation factors.
  7. Self-expanding field formats are also possible instead of fixed values.
  8. To have a valid filtering, please perform any export after the optimization solution took
     place. The filter works in two ways:
        • For a task loop that doesn’t match the criterion, the output is switched off (only for
          the current active task).
          If no loop matches the criterion, or the output is done outside a task, the most recent
          state is being exported in any case.

Remarks:

  1. If the command is specified without parameters, the export process is invoked to the
     default postprocessor as described in the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66).

  2. For possible output formats of each postprocessor, please refer to the detailed description
     in chapter 7.1 ff.

  3. The filename convention for each postprocessor is described in chapter 7.1.1 ff.

  4. The SIMPACK export must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness and mass
     matrices have to be reassembled internally, before invocation of the export process.

  5. The EXCITE export must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness and mass
     matrices have to be reassembled internally, before invocation of the export process.

  6. The SIMDRIVE3D export must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness and
     mass matrices have to be reassembled internally, before invocation of the export process.

Remarks:




                                                                                                      UCI
  1. The range of supported items is postprocessor dependent. A detailed description may be
     found in chapter 7.1 ff.

  2. In contrast to the item command of the -PRINT- section, this command does not invoke
     the output process. It is a pure selection command.

  3. The item selections are valid only for the currently active situation and component. If a
     change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be done again
     since the selectable items (usually) have changed.

  4. If the export commands are grouped within a task, an explicit selection of items may
     be advantageous in order to double–check that all desired results have been computed
     previously.

  5. The creation of a combined model by ITEM TOPO COMBINE is performed in a loop upon
     the whole configuration. Therefore it must not be called within a task. This option is
     supported for PERMAS, PATRAN and IDEAS. For the numbering scheme of the com-
     bined model, please refer to the COMBNUM option of the DEFAULT (see page 2-66 ff.)
     command.

  6. ITEM TOPO COND builds a mathematical model description (only external DOFs) in
     order to represent the substructure only by its coupling matrices.

  7. ITEM TOPO DMODEL creates an artificial model for the verification of the design element
     model topology. Design elements are exported as their finite element equivalent.

  8. ITEM TOPO DESEARCHVOL generates an artificial model for postprocessing of the de-
     sign element search volume. Design elements are exported as there FE element equiva-
     lent.

  9. ITEM TOPO/MODL NEWCOOR selects nodal point coordinates modified by result val-
     ues, depending on the analysis type. Default are displacement results, so a deformed
     model will be written. In case of shape optimization, the coordinate positions of the actual



V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         2-389
0. ITEM TOPO RADSURF selects the coarsened radiation surface (see $ELCOARSE) for
   postprocessing purposes instead of the initial radiation mesh. See also example HT9 on
   page 13-145 ff. of [um550].

1. The output of a partial model (ITEM PART) must be preceded by setting an element set
   filter using the CURRENT ESET command. Additional nodes can be selected by using
   the CURRENT NSET command also. A partial model with corresponding partial results
   will be written.

2. ITEM HULL selects all elements that reside on the hull of the model, hence a reduction
   is achieved mainly if solid elements are used. A partial model with corresponding hull
   results will be written.

3. If the hull created by HGEN shall be output (e.g. after a topology or shape optimization),
   ITEM TOPO SMOOTH is to be used.

4. ELEMENT COG must be explicitly requested and can be exported only to PERMAS.

5. Laminate stresses in the ply system are available only in PERMAS format. Element
   stresses must have been calculated previously by the GENerate ELement STRESS com-
   mand.

6. The weight summary item is only deselectable. It is exclusively available for the PERMAS
   postprocessing format.

7. Modal accelerations, displacements and velocities must be explicitly selected for export.

8. With option BOOK, a non-standard result may be selected, e.g. created with the RESULT
   option of a preceding UCI command. If the result is of complex arithmetic type and should
   be exported as complex result, the option COMPLEX must be used instead. Here the
   name of the amplitude book must be specified.

ample:

ase refer to example OP5V1 of [um550] for the use of ITEM COOR CHANGE and ITEM
DL NEWCOOR.

   since the selectable items usually have changed.

Remarks:

  1. The range of supported items is postprocessor dependent. A detailed description may be
     found in chapter 7.1 ff.

  2. In contrast to the item command of the -PRINT- section, this command does not invoke
     the output process. It is a pure selection process.

  3. The item selections are valid only for the currently active situation and component. If a
     change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be done again
     since the selectable items usually have changed.

  4. If the export process is grouped within a task, a selection of items may be advantageous
     in order to verify that all desired results have been computed previously.

  5. The MHIS xy-data contains one curve for the maximum relative constraint violation in
     percent, as well as one or two curves with the maximum and/or minimum absolute con-
     straint values for each $DCONSTRAINT (see page 3-900 ff.) definition (depending on the
     specification of upper and/or lower limit).

forms an export of a condensed topology and optionally the matrix model of the current
ution.

marks:

1. The functionality is restricted to the solutions:

      • STATIC
      • VIBRATION ANALYSIS
        For SOLV = MLDR, only CONF = TOP (/KEEP) is supported. A full backtransforma-
        tion is not meaningful for this purpose.
      • FSCOUPLED VIBRATION ANALYSIS (dry condensation)
        The SOLV = MLDR option is not supported

   For other solutions Guyan condensation matrices are selected.




02                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                        V 19.00.287
  3. Allows to postprocess results also in the mathematical subcomponent model. A reduced
     backtransformation is possible by the result variant parameters $PARAMETER (see page
     3-1057 ff.) with options RFILTER/REFILTER. In case of a dynamic condensation, a con-
     densed model is being created for the external modes of the component.

  4. In addition to the matrices, a condensed model is being created for the external dofs and
     the local dofs of the component. The option allows to hide the physical model but for
     optimum performance, the ORIG option is recommended.

  5. The functionality ist restricted to internally partitioned books. The selected node range
     has to be chosen using the EXPORT CURRENT (see page 2-365 ff.) command.




                                                                                                   EXPORT
  6. The data objects are written according to the parameters given in the OPEN command
     (OPEN (see page 2-403 ff.)), or the default settings of the OPEN command are used.




                                                                                                     UCI
     Only PERMAS Format is supported for this functionality.

  7. The requested data object must exist.

  8. Degree of freedom information refers to possibly rotated node basis. (Component system
     if no rotated basis).

  9. The backtransformation matrix may be very huge, depending on the number of local and
     external dofs. Hence, it may be more efficient to re-compute the matrix in subsequent
     runs.

 10. For fscoupled vibration analysis, please perform a structural weight analysis before invok-
     ing the matrix model command.

 11. Following parameter can be set for a modified selection of data

        • DRYCOND PRESSURE
        • LOAD MATRIX

     For a detailed description see EXPORT PARAM (see page 2-405 ff.) command.

 12. For the selected elements, an output of plot elements is being performed in the artificial
     model. If the NSET parameter is used, an element is only output, if all element nodes are
     a part of the node set.

Remarks:

  1. A duplicate node may be removed if all dofs are being declared as external, i.e. no local
     results exist. The CCNODES option helps to reduce the size of the result output of a

     combined model.




                                                                                                      UCI
  2. CRULE sets the preference for keeping identifiers in a combined model (ITEM TOPO
     COMBINE). The applicability of a rule is postprocessor dependent. Please have a look in
     the interface description for further information.

  3. The sets are created by the PRETEST (see page 2-315 ff.) command.

  4. By DRYCOND all pressure dof dependent data for a dry condensation can be switched
     off during the export with the EXPORT MATRIX (see page 2-399 ff.) command.

        • The Craig Bampton matrix for the pressure dofs will not be written on the matrix file.
        • The CBSOLV parameter and the local dofs of the doftype pressure is also not written
          to the post file for the ARTIFICIAL method of the matrix model export.

  5. The export of load matrices (BQM, BQH ...) can be switched off during the export with
     the EXPORT MATRIX (see page 2-399 ff.) command.

  6. Number of digits for float values of model data on PERMAS export files POST or DATO.
     The default value is the value of the DEFAULT SET MODEL_DIGITS switch.

  7. Number of digits for float values of results on PERMAS export file POST.

  8. Reduce the amount of data for the pressure result. FLUID DOFS = ALL writes values for
     all degrees of fredom of the pressure result.

  9. Reduce the amount of data for displacement, velocity and acceleration results. MECHAN-
     ICAL DOFS = ALL writes values for all degrees of fredom of the displacement, velocity
     and acceleration results, if possible for the selected post processor format.

 10. Send the units to postprocessing file. Currently only used for the I-DEAS MASTER_SERIES
     file. The given units are the units of the model. It is no conversion of any data performed!

The input to finite element systems may contain a large amount of data. To handle those data
in a user convenient and clearly structured manner the PERMAS data input was developed
following some fundamental concepts:

   • Uniform syntax
      Input lines for all kind of data and, as far as possible, UCI commands follow the same
     syntax rules.

   • Block structure
      Data are input in blocks, i.e. a header line describing data type, input options etc., and
     lines with input data. Data blocks are assigned to components, variants etc. by enclosing




                                                                                                    DAT
     them with bracket lines. The sequence the data blocks are input is of no importance for
     the computation.

   • Separation of material data
      Input data for PERMAS are split up into component-dependent data, i.e. mesh definition,
     constraints, loads etc., and component-independent material data. Materials are defined
     by data blocks describing all needed material properties, and are referenced by their
     names within component-dependent input.

   • Identifiers
      Node identifiers, element identifiers etc. can be chosen in an arbitrary manner but have to
     be unique within one component. Performance and internal data structure do not depend
     on the numbers used as identifiers.

   • Set concept
     Sets are used to group together elements or nodes. Sets are identified by names, and in
     most cases where properties, loads etc. are assigned a set name instead of the identifier
     of a single element or node may be used.

   • Data input convention
      In contrast to earlier versions of PERMAS the zero/overwrite convention is no longer
     valid. All necessary data have to be input with the only exception that in some cases
     trailing zeroes may be omitted. Overwriting of input data by new input is never possible.


3.1.1 Partition of Data Input

The data input to PERMAS consists of text lines in a sequential file which are arranged in data
blocks, enclosed by brackets of different level. High level brackets $ENTER ... $EXIT enclose
component-dependent data for one component as well as component-independent data, e.g.
material data. Medium level brackets $name ... $END name enclose data blocks which e.g.
belong to the same variant of one component. Data blocks itself consist of a data block header

Logical Lines consist of one or more physical lines, the first of which is the starting line, the
remaining lines are continuation lines. Logical lines are handled internally as one input entity,
but nevertheless splitting of items is not allowed, i.e. each item must start and end on the same
physical line. Comments are not part of logical lines.


Continuation Lines are physical lines which are marked with an ampersand (&) as first non-
blank character.




                                                                                                    DAT
Header Lines contain a dollar sign ($) as first non-blank character. They are used as data block
header lines, bracket header or delimiter lines and for control purposes. Header lines (except
$ECHO) may have any number of continuation lines. The general syntax of header lines is
given by


                                                                  ∗
          $key              parameter              assignment




where key contains the header key.


Data Lines contain as first non-blank character neither a dollar sign ($) nor an ampersand (&)
nor an exclamation mark (!). They are used to input data within data blocks and may contain
any number of continuation lines. The general syntax of data lines is given by:

Some items are only valid for User Control Interface, data input or output.


Tuples are items, separated by commas:

tuple    :=     tuple(item)      :=    item [, item ]∗


A List contains tuples, separated by blanks:

list    :=    list(tuple)   :=    tuple [ tuple ]∗


Lists are separated by a colon. If tuples contain more than one item, then one tuple of a list
may contain items of different types, but each tuple in one list must have the same number of
items, and corresponding items of tuples in one list must have the same type.


An Assignment is defined by

assignment        :=    parameter = list


where parameter is an item of type name.

ut variables with fixed integer indices (e.g. SITNAM(3)) may be used as constant items
 where in the current input stream whereas input variables with index expression may be

he definition of the loop variable by
                                     lpvar = iS , iE
h the name of the loop variable lpvar, the start value iS which must be greater than zero,
d the end value iE which must be greater than or equal iS . The generation loop starts with
ar = iS , and after each loop lpvar is incremented by one, therefore the loop is executed
 − iS + 1)-times.
 hin a loop, input variables may be used to replace any integer, real, double precision or
me item. The input variable is inserted as varnam(ind) where ind is an index expression of

                                  [c1 ∗] v1 [± [ci ∗] vi ] [± c0 ]
ere ci are integer constants and vi are loop variables. The value varnam(ind) replaces then
 original value in the data line.
y number of input variables may defined, but the definition may not be done within a loop,

marks:

1. Situations are defined within the top component of a configuration. A single component
   is always the top component.

2. The situation name is mandatory and must be unique within one configuration. If a data
   line is present and the component name is missing, then the data line specifications hold
   for the current component.

3. If for a situation a variant is not assigned explicitly but needed, the default variant (DFLTC-
   NST, DFLTSYST, DFLTLOAD, DFLTMOD or DFLTRES) is used. Default variants must not
   be specified explicitly. If only default variants are used the data line of the situation defini-
   tion may be omitted.

4. Up to now, structure block variants should be used only for the generalized dynamic
   condensation as presented in examples DEVX8V1 to DEVX8V3, the Mixed Boundary
   Craig-Bampton Method.

5. Situation definition is closed by an (optional) $END SITUATION line or by a new compo-
   nent input medium level bracket line or by any high level bracket line.

6. If parameter PARENT is specified, the data block defines the child situation name of par-
   ent situation parent. Child situations make use of results of the corresponding parent
   situation (e.g. modal methods need the eigenmodes of the system) and have i.g. the
   same system and constraint variants as the parent situation. For exceptions see remark
   8.
   Child situations may be connected to other situations, but situations where connections
   are specified must be non-child situations, therefore parameter CONNECTED is not avail-
   able if parameter PARENT is specified.

7. The following variants may be selected within definition of a (parent) situation without
   parameter CONNECTED:

       • Constraint, system, loading and result variants of top or single component.
       • Constraint variants for all subcomponents of the configuration.

     System variants of subcomponents are selected by a $SUBVAR data block within sys-
     tem variant definition, see page 3-556, loading variants by a $SUBVAR data block within
     loading variant definition, see page 3-876, and modification variants by a $SUBVAR data
     block within modification variant definition, see page 3-996.


 8                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                             V 19.00.287
     already defined by corresponding parent situation. System variants for child situations
     containing modal transient or modal frequency response analyses may only be specified
     if the system variant of the parent situation is inserted into the system variant of the child
     situation, see $INSERT VARIANT, page 3-525. Loading variants of subcomponents are




                                                                                                      Situation
     selected by a $SUBVAR data block within loading variant definition, see page 3-876.




                                                                                                        DAT
  9. If parameter CONNECTED is specified:
        • System and modification variants for top or single components of situations control-
          ling design optimization
     All situations connected to one specific design optimization must contain the same sys-
     tem variant or a different system variant where the common system variant is inserted,
     see $INSERT VARIANT, page 3-525. Collector situations (see remark 10) may not be
     connected.
 10. If parameter ASSEMBLY is specified, all referred situations must have:
        • the same system variant
        • the same result variant
     as the collector situation. The collector situation itself does not store results, but dis-
     tributes the results back to the referred situations. It must have a different loading variant
     as the referred situations. The definition is currently usable for modal frequency response
     analyses only and cannot be used in combination with optimization.
     Please refer to Example DRA3V2 of [um550] on page 9-78 ff.

marks:

1. ALLOCATE data blocks are used to input user-specified data for further access.

2. User-specified data may be allocated to nodes or elements.

3. User-specified data must be unique, i.e. for one name datnam and one node or element
   only one tuple of data may be specified.

4. Empty node or element sets are not allowed.

5. User-specified data are stored internally in composed tables with names NY<datnam>.UDAT
   for nodes and EY<datnam>.UDAT for elements. To assure uniqueness, datnam must not
   have more than five characters.

6. If DSTYPE = SCALAR (default) is specified, a set of ncol scalar values is allocated.

7. If DSTYPE = VECTOR is specified, one or more vectors are allocated, and the number
   of columns ncol must be a multiple of three.

8. If the input for one data object is splitted into more than one $ALLOCATE data block, then
   the column titles, if any, must be specified in the first one.

9. Each data line may have up to ncol data. Trailing zeroes may be omitted.

0. The floating point data are stored internally in actual precision in any case.

Remarks:

  1. Basic variables may be defined only in single or top components. Their identifiers must
     be unique within the component.



V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          3-29
    by input, it is generated internally.

4. The type of a basic variable defines the type of uncertain entities the basic variable may
   be applied on. In pure reliability analysis, the following types are available:

       • Design parameter: The basic variable is used as design variable influencing prop-
         erties of the FE-model. The corresponding design variable defined by $DELEMENT
         (see page 3-58 ff.) or $DSVNODE (see page 3-90 ff.) must have the same identi-
         fier (bsvid = dsvid). Mean values of basic variables are used as initial values of the
         design variables, input of initial values of design variables by $DSVVAL (see page
         3-401 ff.) is not possible. Furthermore, design variables representing basic variables
         must not be made dependent by linking, see $DSVLINK (see page 3-87 ff.).
       • Load factor: The basic variable is used as multiplier for a load pattern to define
         a stochastic load. The link between basic variable and load pattern is defined by
         $COMBINE LOADS (see page 3-562 ff.) in the corresponding loading variant.
       • Parameter of another basic variable: Each parameter of a probability distribution
         function may be a non-deterministic value itself, described by a basic variable. A
         basic variable used as parameter of another basic variable must be included in
         the definition of the probability distribution function of the other basic variable, see
         $PDFUNCTION (see page 3-208 ff.), replacing function parameters. A basic variable
         depending on parameters replaced by basic variables may not be used as parameter
         of another basic variable itself.
       • State function parameter: The basic variable is used as direct parameter of the limit
         state function. It must be included in the z-vector, see $ZVECTOR (see page 3-1110
         ff.).

    In combined optimization and reliability analysis, the following type is available in addition:

       • Stochastic properties of a deterministic design variable: A basic variable is estab-
         lished as stochastic design parameter where its mean value is given by a corre-
         sponding (deterministic) design variable with the same identifier (bsvid = dsvid). The
         initial value of the design variable is given by the mean value in the corresponding
         probability distribution function and must not be specified by $DSVVAL (see page
         3-401 ff.).
         The probability distribution function itself (see $PDFUNCTION (see page 3-208 ff.))
         must be specified by statistical values (DATA = MOMENTS).

5. The probability distribution function associated with a basic variable must be defined by
   $PDFUNCTION (see page 3-208 ff.).

ample:

         &    DESCRIPTION=’Actual Thickness of part 1’

marks:

1. Contact regions may be locked according to the contact results of a referenced situation.
   The locking is done by an implicit generation of multipoint constraints on all contact nodes
   that match a corresponding locking condition:
      • For Node-To-Node or Surface-To-Node contacts the DOFs of the 2nd contact partner
        will be defined as dependents of the DOFs from the 1st contact partner.
      • For Node-To-Ground or Surface-To-Ground contacts the DOFs of the 1st contact
        partner will be defined as suppressed or dependent according to their local ROTB
        system.
      • Surface-To-Surface coupling works perfectly well for contact analysis, but may cause
        cyclic MPC dependencies if both sides request mutual locks to opposing patches.
        Therefore Surface-To-Surface contacts are not recommended to be used together
        with contact locking, i.e. those contacts should be downgraded to a unique Surface-
        To-Node contact definition.

2. The contact locking request is part of the component definition, and is valid for all situa-
   tions of this component.

3. Contact labels cadef refer to $CONTACT definitions in the constraint variant of the refer-
   enced situation refsit in referenced component refcomp. Pretension label ptdef refer to
   $PRETENSION definitions with GUIDING=CONTACT in the structure block of the refer-
   enced component refcomp.

4. Contact locking requests must be unique, e.g. for contact label cadef only one specifi-
   cation (only one data line) is possible. Moreover pretension labels must be unique with
   respect to contact label. In case a pretension label matches a contact label the pretension
   definition must be distinguished with a PRETEN_ prefix, e.g. PRETEN_MIX for preten-
   sion definition MIX (the PRETEN_ prefix can be used in any case, so it is good practice
   to use it even if both name spaces are separate).

5. With the CASFILE option a consolidated contact situation together with a matching con-
   tact status file is sufficient as reference, i.e. at least a TASK STORE of e.g. STATIC [TO
   PRECHECK] is needed in the reference situation, but there is no need for an actual static
   analysis as the referred ’results’ are read from the given contact status file. The contact
   names/ids and nodal point IDs in the file must match the contact names/ids and nodes in
   the reference situation, i.e. the file must match the reference contact topology exactly (a
   variant’s template is not sufficient). However, the cas-file may contain pure normal contact


4                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           V 19.00.287
     that no anisotropic friction is involved.

  6. If contact locking is requested and no specific contact or pretension labels are specified
     at all, i.e. there is only one data block $CONTLOCK, and this data block contains only
     the first data line, then all contacts and pretensions (with GUIDING=CONTACT) of the
     referenced situation are taken into account. The same is true if there is a second data
     line but without contact label, only with parameter NORMAL and/or FRICTION.

  7. If any contact is specified, then only the specified contacts are taken into account.

  8. Coupling in the normal direction of contact is controlled by parameter NORMAL:




                                                                                                       Structure
        • If NORMAL = FREE is specified, then the displacements in the normal direction
          are always uncoupled.




                                                                                                         DAT
        • If NORMAL = LOCK_IF_ACTIVE (default) is specified, then the displacements in
          the normal direction are coupled if the contact is active.
        • For NORMAL = LOCK is specified, then the displacements in the normal direction
          are always coupled (independent of contact status).

  9. Any NORMAL condition (apart from NORMAL=FREE) may be extended by an additional
     limit condition with a threshold value that must be matched before a corresponding LOCK
     is actually established, see remark 13 below.

 10. In the tangential plane, coupling is possible only if the current dof type establishes at least
     3 DOFs per node (i.e. DOFTYPE=DISP) and if friction was taken into account by the
     referred $CONTACT definition. Then the coupling is controlled by parameter FRICTION:
        • If FRICTION = FREE (default) is specified, then the displacements in the tangen-
          tial plane are always uncoupled.
        • If FRICTION = LOCK_IF_ACTIVE is specified, then the displacements in the tan-
          gential plane are coupled if the contact is active (see ROTB restrictions below).
        • If FRICTION = LOCK_IF_STICK is specified, then the displacements in the tan-
          gential plane are coupled only if the contact is in stick (see ROTB restrictions below).
        • If FRICTION = LOCK is specified, then the displacements in the tangential plane
          are coupled in any case (independent of contact status, see restrictions below).
        • For FRICTION = MATRICES the displacements in the tangential plane are uncou-
          pled (like FRICTION=FREE), but will lead to additional damping matrices needed for
          some special dynamic analysis (e.g. brake-squeal analysis).

 11. FRICTION = MATRICES is only allowed for DOFTYPE=DISP and in combination with
     NORMAL = LOCK_IF_ACTIVE (default).

 12. Any FRICTION condition (apart from FRICTION=FREE) may be extended by an addi-
     tional limit condition with a threshold value that must be matched before a corresponding
     LOCK is actually established, see remark 13 below.


V 19.00.287                    PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           3-35
             MINPRESS        pN min    R          minimum normal contact pressure
             MINSHEAR        pF min    R ≥ 0.0    minimum fritcional shear
             MINFORCE        RN min    R          minimum normal contact force
             MINFRICF        RF min    R ≥ 0.0    minimum frictional force
             MAXGAP           δmax     R          maximum gap width
             MAXSLIP          δslip    R ≥ 0.0    maximum slip distance

    Options MAXGAP and MAXSLIP are not supported in combination with the CASFILE pa-
    rameter (see remark 5).

    Also note that the frictional conditions (MINSHEAR, MINFRICF, MAXSLIP) may be used
    only if friction was taken into account and that limit values < 0.0 (for MINPRESS, MIN-
    FORCE, MAXGAP) are meaningfull only if the referred contact enforces active normal
    state by a corresponding LOCK, FIXED or FORCE parameter (see $CONTACT LOAD for
    details). Moreover, MAXGAP condition is usually only meaningfull together with NOR-
    MAL/FRICTION=LOCK.

4. If a colon separated list of nodes is appended to the lock condition line then the given
   condition applies only to those contact nodes that are part of the extra list (instead of just
   all nodes of the corresponding contact definition). Node set names refer to the current
   component (nodal point identifiers as well as local ROTB systems of those nodes must
   match in current and reference component).


ample:

 COMPONENT=kompo_1 SITUATION=situ_0
 CA1 NORMAl=LOCK,MAXGAP,0.1                            ! Lock CA1 if gap width <= 0.1
 CA2 FRICTION=LOCK_IF_ACTIVE,MINPRESS,100.0            ! Lock if active & CAPRESS>=100.0
 PreTen_BOLT NORMAL=LOCK                               ! Lock pretension BOLT

ONTLOCK

 cnt_456 FRICTION=LOCK_IF_STICK          : n_456_part       ! for nset n_456_part in

2. Nodal point identifiers must be unique within one component.

3. Duplicate input of nodal points is accepted if the node coordinates are identical within the
   tolerance given by the TOLNOD parameter.

4. Inaccurate nodal point coordinates may be trimmed by TRIMCOOR.

5. Trailing zeros in list of coordinates may be omitted.

6. If the data line contains a nodal point set instead of float coordinates, then the nodal point
   coordinates xg are generated from the barycenter rule as a mean value of all coordinates
   in the set, i.e.:
                              1X                  1X                  1X
                        xg =      xn ,      yg =       yn ,      zg =      zn
                             n n                  n n                 n n

7. Generated nodes must not be used to generate other ones.

   reference system is used the same reference system must be used for all $COOR and
   $TRIMCOOR definitions of this node, too.

0. All nodes with displacement, temperature or pressure degrees of freedom are automat-
   ically assigned to nodesets NODEDISP, NODETEMP, NODEPRES or NODEPOTE, re-
   spectively.

                             nset




Remarks:

  1. Nodal point identifiers must be unique within one component.

  2. Generation rule BARYCENTER means that the generated node is located at the barycen-
     ter of specified nodes which is defined as the mean value of the coordinates, i.e. it holds
     for the coordinates xg of the generated node

                                    1X                      1X                    1X
                            xg =        xn ,         yg =       yn ,       zg =       zn
                                    n n                     n n                   n n

  3. At least one node must be specified, multiple occurence of the same node is ignored.

  4. Generated nodes must not be defined otherwise, i.e. they must not be included in a
     $COOR data block.

  5. Generated nodes must not be used for the definition of local reference systems by $RSYS
     data blocks.


V 19.00.287                        PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                        3-39
9. The coordinates of generated nodes are calculated during consolidation. Afterwards they
   are handled just as any other node, i.e. the coordinates may be modified by coordinate
   update in geometric nonlinear analyses or shape optimization etc.

0. All nodes with displacement, temperature or pressure degrees of freedom are automat-
   ically assigned to nodesets NODEDISP, NODETEMP, NODEPRES or NODEPOTE, re-
   spectively.

ample:

Remarks:




                                                                                                Structure
  1. The name of the book is built according to name.ext if an extension is specified; if the
     book name has no extension, the name is given by name and must not contain a period




                                                                                                  DAT
     (.) as last character.

  2. The global dimension of matrices may be specified equal to the number of degrees of
     freedom of selected families. Following selections are available:

                        doffam             Freedom Family
                        LOCAL              Local degrees of freedom
                        EXTERNAL           External degrees of freedom
                        PRESCRIBED         Prescribed degrees of freedom
                        SUPPRESSED         Suppressed degrees of freedom
                        DEPENDENT          Dependent degrees of freedom
                        ALLFAM             All degree of freedom families;
                                           for Boolean matrices only.

  3. If the extension ext of the book name represents one of the doftypes DISP, TEMP, PRES
     or POTE, then the doftypes in row and column direction are given by that doftype, and
     specification is not necessary. If, however, the extension ext represents the doftype
     MATH, then then the doftypes in row and column direction may be specified explicitly.
     The default doftype in row and column direction is always given by the extension ext.

  4. Following matrix formats are available:

                                   iform   Matrix format
                                   R       Rectangular
                                   D       Diagonal
                                   DS      Diagonal-symmetric

Important notice:
The following data line description is only valid for general purpose design element types like
DBEAM, DQUAD4, DHEXE8 etc. (for a complete list see page 5-3).
Even though the general purpose design elements have the capability for shape and topology
optimization, it is highly recommended to use the specialized design element types DSHAPE,




                                                                                                                    Structure
DBEAD, DNODE or DFREE for shape and DTOPO for topology optimization instead.

deid         I>0             Design element identifier.
dsvid        I>0             Design variable identifier.
dsvset     name/text         Design variable set name, see remark 9.

eid          I>0             Element identifier.

Remarks:

  1. Design elements may be defined only in single or top components. Their identifiers must
     be unique within the component.

  2. Design elements are used to define the modification for those properties of the assigned
     elements which depend on the design variables. For shape optimization they define the
     coordinate modifications for all nodes connected to the assigned elements.




V 19.00.287                         PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                                     3-59
        elements, see $DVGPAR and $DVMPAR. If the specification of design variables is
        done by a set dsvset, the set must exist (must not be empty).
      • Design variables used for shape optimization are not specified within the design
        element. Instead they are connected to the design nodes, see $DSVNODE and
        describe node coordinate modifications, see $DVCOOR.
      • Design variables used for topology optimization must be specified by list(dsvid . . .)
        or set dsvset. If ASSIGN = ELEMENT is specified, they are assigned to elements
        one by one. For ASSIGN = DIRECT the (one and only one) design variable is valid
        for the whole design element, and is assigned to all corresponding elements. The
        design variables describe element filling ratios, see $DVTPAR. If design variable set
        dsvset is empty (not otherwise defined), then it is established internally, see remark
        9.
4. For pure sizing or topology optimization, the list of design nodes list(dnid) may be omitted.
   For shape optimization, it must be specified in any case.
5. Design variables used for shape optimization are assigned to each related design ele-
   ment.
6. Design variable identifiers must be unique within the configuration.
7. Any element may be assigned to only one design element.
8. For sizing problems, the design element and all elements assigned to it must have the
   same type of Geometrical Data Record.
9. Design variables may be specified by a set dsvset. For sizing the set must exist. For
   topology optimization with ASSIGN = ELEMENT the set may be empty (not otherwise
   defined), and the corresponding design variables are generated internally, one design
   variable for each element.
0. If ASSIGN = ELEMENT is specified (available for topology optimization only), the design
   variables are assigned to the connected elements one by one, i.e. the number of design
   variables equals the number of connected elements. The sequence of elements is ac-
   cording to ascending element identifiers, the corresponding sequence of assigned design
   variables is the sequence of appearance in list(dsvid) or the sequence within set dsvset.
   A unambiguous assignment may be achieved by an ordered design variable set.
1. If ELEMENTS = AUTO is specified, then the geometry of the design element defines the
   finite elements to be assigned, i.e. all finite elements in the neighborhood of the design
   element with types corresponding to the type of the design element are assigned to that
   design element automatically. The list of element identifiers on input line must be omitted.
   The element types corresponding to the type of a design element are listed for each
   design element type in the design element atlas, see page 5-1 ff.. The design element
   search volume for automatic element assignement can be verified by EXPORT ITEM
   TOPO DESEARCHVOL.


0                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           V 19.00.287
 13. Parameter OUTTOL is used to control the assignment of finite elements near to the
     boundary of design elements. If ELEMENTS = AUTO is specified, a finite element near
     to the boundary is assigned, if the distance of the center of gravity from the boundary is
     less than OUTTOL ∗LE where LE is a typical length of the design element. If not input,
     the default value defined by global system key OUTTOL is used.

 14. Additional check results for design model properties can be provided for output in post-
     processor format by DEFAULT SET MODEL = VERIFICATION (refer to DEFAULT SET
     remark 4 for further information).

Remarks:

    1. Design element restraint specifications are possible only in single or top components and
       are available for the following design element types:

                          DSHAPE     DBEAD      DNODE       DFREE      DTOPO      other types
             CONST          yes        yes        no          no         no
             LINEAR         yes        no         no          no         no
             BOUND          yes      only C0      no        only C0      no
             FREEZE         no         no         no          no        yes
             LAYER          no         no         no          no        yes
             PRINT3D        no         no         no          yes       yes


V 19.00.287                     PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                            3-79
3. Up to three restraints of TYPE = CONST or TYPE = LINEAR may be defined. They must
   share the same reference system with different axes for each restraint. They may also be
   combined with a $DESYMM specification as long as this combination keeps unambigous
   and consistent.

4. By default, at least a C0-continuity condition is fulfilled at the design element boundary,
   i.e. the sub-range of its hull which is connected to finite elements outside the design
   element. Further ranges of the hull or higher continuity conditions may be applied with a
   restraint definition of TYPE = BOUND.

5. Frozen regions can be defined to enforce accretion of material within topology optimiza-
   tion. The usage of this restraint is restricted to design elements of type DTOPO (see
   page 3-71) and applies only for default parameter TOPOVAR = MAPPED or NODAL, see
   STARTUP section command DEFAULT (see page 2-66 ff.).

6. Layer restraints serve to define equality or inequality constraints on functions of topo
   design variables in different layers, i.e. by multiple definition of DTOPO design elements
   to the same finite element set. Hence all design elements referred by the specified design
   element set must be of type DTOPO and must be defined for the same element set (see
   page 3-71). The number of items in the design element set must match the number of
   arguments of the specified function.

7. The PRINT3D must not be combined with $RELDIR definitions. Additionally:
   Only for DTOPO design elements: The PRINT3D restraint is only available for default
   parameter TOPOVAR = NODAL, see STARTUP section command DEFAULT (see page
   2-66 ff.).
   Only for DFREE design elements: the MAXTHICK value is ignored.

 applications of design element restraints see examples OP5V1, OP16, OP17 and TOPO8
um550].

$DERESTRAINT TYPE = CONST              ! constant shape deformation
  1001 RSYS = 21 AXIS = 1              ! along x’ of reference system 21

Remarks:

  1. Design element symmetry specifications are possible only in single or top components,
     and are only available for design element type DSHAPE (see page 3-68), DBEAD (see
     page 3-62) and DTOPO (see page 3-71).
  2. The reference system used for symmetry specification may be also be a cyclic or spherical
     system. Nevertheless, in any case the axes of the corresponding cartesian system at the
     origin are used to define symmetry.
  3. The axes-definition in the data line have the following meaning depending on symmetry
     type:
          • PLANAR: axes define symmetry plane through origin.
          • AXI: axis defines rotation axis.
          • CYCLIC: first axis defines rotational axis, second axis defines starting point for first
            sector (counted counterclockwise).
  4. SECTSYM = YES within a cyclic symmetry definition additionally enforces planar sym-
     metry with respect to the angle bisectors.
  5. Design element symmetry definitions may be combined with each other. All definitions for
     one design element must share the same reference system. Up to three planar symme-
     tries with orthogonal symmetry planes may be defined. Cyclic and axial symmetry may
     be combined with a planar symmetry, where the symmetry plane must be orthogonal to
     the rotation axis.

marks:

1. Linking of design variables is used to establish dependencies between design variables
   which are assigned to design elements. Definition of additional design variables by linking
   is not possible.

2. Dependent design variables cannot be used in other design variable linking relations as
   dependent variables.

3. If SAME is specified, all dependent design variables are equal to the independent design
   variable.

4. If LINEAR is specified, the dependent design variable y is given according to
                                            X
                                        y=      ci xi
                                                 i

    as a linear function of the independent design variables x.

5. If GENERAL is specified, the linking relation is given by

                                    y = fun(xi , i = 1, nof var)

    where y is the dependent design variable, xi , i = 1, nof var are nof var independent
    design variables and fun(xi ) is a function with nof var independent variables.

6. Functions are defined within a $FUNCTION data block, see page 3-1112 ff..

7. For functions used for design variable linking the first derivative must be available.

V 19.00.287                        PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         3-99
marks:

1. Global element system definitions which are inputted by $ELSYS within the $STRUCTURE
   bracket, are inserted into the geometrical data records of the referenced elements in all
   system variants, see $GEODAT.

2. The definition of local element systems is possible only if the geometrical data record of
   each referenced element contains the field PREF, REFSYS or REFSYSX resp., or for
   gasket elements, see remark 3. With the exception of POINT and RSYS, the specifi-
   cation made on header line must match the field in the geometrical data record of each
   referenced element. For that, and for the rules to establish the local element system see
   element description.

3. For gasket elements, the definition of element systems with option POINTS or RSYS is
   optional, and must be done within the $STRUCTURE bracket. We remark that the z’ axis
   (3) of the element system must coincide with the through-the-thickness direction.

4. Local element systems which may be defined via REFSYS or REFSYSX resp. can be es-
   tablished by three points (or two points resp.), see pictures below, using the specification
   POINTS, or can be derived from a reference system, see remark 6, if RSYS is specified.

5. Beam element systems are established using a reference point PREF. This reference
   point may be determined with reference to a system defined by three points, using the
   specification POINTS, see picture below, or to a reference system, see remark 6, if RSYS
   is specified. In any case, the direction from the center of gravity of the first beam section
   to the reference point is given by the direction of the first coordinate axis of the reference
   system (local cartesian system for cylindrical or spherical reference system).

6. If RSYS is specified on header line, the given reference system rsys is used to estab-
   lish the local element system. Reference systems are defined by data blocks $RSYS or
   $RSYSAX resp. for axisymmetric structures. RSYS = 0 means component system.
   For cylindrical or spherical reference systems the local cartesian system for the orienta-
   tion of the local element system is generated using the generation rules defined on page
   1-11.
   If parameter AXES is omitted, the local element system coincides with the local cartesian
   system, else idof x specifies the axis of the local cartesian system which is used as x-axis
   of the element system, and idof y specifies the axis of the local cartesian system which
   is used as y-axis of the element system. Following values may be used:
      1     (-1) : Positive (negative) x-axis of reference system (r-axis for axisymmetric struc-
                   tures).
      2     (-2) : Positive (negative) y-axis of reference system (z-axis for axisymmetric struc-
                   tures).



00                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           V 19.00.287

     $ELSYS within the $STRUCTURE bracket, by $ELSYS in the $SYSTEM variant or by
     $GEODAT.

  8. The coordinates of points may be given in the component system (default) or in any other
     reference system rsys, which may be a cartesian, cylindrical or spherical one.

  9. Angles must be input in degrees.

      existing sets by $ESET is not possible.

      $ELEMENT data blocks.

   4. In one set any item may appear only once; any further appearance in the list will be
      ignored.

   6. If RULE = RANGE is specified the set contains all existing elements with identifiers eid1 ≤

      Each data item occurs only once in a set.

marks:

1. External degrees of freedom form a separate degree of freedom family. Within the cur-
   rent (sub-)component they cannot be suppressed or prescribed nor used as dependent
   degrees of freedom in MPC’s.

2. Rotated bases at nodes with external degrees of freedom have to be declared via $ROTB
   within $STRUCTURE brackets. They should be used with care because the user is re-
   sponsible for the proper orientation of corresponding node bases in sub- and hypercom-
   ponent.

3. For dynamic reduction, eigenmodes are used as generalized degrees of freedom. They
   are assigned to special degrees of freedom at nodes which are declared as external. The
   following assignments are available:

                                  dof type     degree of freedom
                                   DISP                9
                                   PRES                3

4. A node to which an eigenmode is assigned may not be used in element or MPC defini-
   tions, i.e. it may not carry any other degrees of freedom.

5. If MODE is specified, the associated nodal points must be kept separate for the hyper-
   component insertion.

6. The reference to a foreign situation is used only for the generalized dynamic condensation
   as presented in examples DEVX8V1 to DEVX8V3, the Mixed Boundary Craig-Bampton
   Method, where the eigenmodes for the condensation are calculated in the foreign instead
   of the active situation.

7. MPC definitions at nodes with external degrees of freedom have to be declared within
   $STRUCTURE brackets.

Remarks:

  1. Reference to a global system is allowed only on basic or single component level.
  2. The $GSYS data block defines position and orientation of the component with respect to
     an assumed global system, i.e. the component system used for the input of the compo-
     nent coincides with the system defined on data line.
  3. The system definition itself refer to the assumed global system, i.e. the coordinates of
     points used for system specification refer always to the assumed global reference system,
     and determine position and orientation of the input component system with respect to the
     assumed global reference system.
  4. During the consolidation process, all corresponding data of the component are trans-
     formed to a new component system which coincides with the assumed global coordinate
     system. After that, e.g. for model output, all component data refer to that new component
     system.
  5. Only one global system reference is possible within a component.
  6. If the relation between global and component system is a pure translation, then it is pos-
     sible to specify TRKIND = TRANS, and only the origin of the system must be input. For
     axisymmetric discretization, only a translation along the zC -axis is possible.
  7. If TRKIND = COMPLETE is specified, i.e. the component system may be rotated with
     respect to the global system, then the following restrictions exist:
          • If a node carries dofs of type DISP or POTE, and the dofs are not in the same degree
            of freedom family, a rotated basis must be assigned to the nodal point. Example: dof
            1 is dependent, dof 2 and 3 are local.


V 19.00.287                       PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                        3-113
        • If for elements with optional reference system (GEDA field REFSYS for elements like
          SPRING6, MASS6 etc.) the reference system is not defined and the local system of
          the first element node is used instead, then that node must have a rotated basis in
          any case.
        • All nodes which are loaded with concentrated loads by $CONLOAD, must have ro-
          tated bases or the concentrated load must be defined with respect to a reference
          system (RSYS > 0).
        • Element loads with components referring to component system may not have any
          functional dependency.

8. For definition of the coordinate system relation see figures below. A general description
   of coordinate systems in PERMAS can be found on page 1-11 ff..
