Figure F3-21: MAXDIST and MAXANGLE define the search space for a weld connection

9. If MPCTYPE = WLS is specified, the connection of the surfaces to the nodes in the
   corresponding sets is done according to the rules valid for the WLSSURFACE connection,
   see $MPC WLSSURFACE. It is done as follows:


72                       PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                      V 19.00.287
        • At least all nodes of one patch of the surface are taken into account.
        • Parameters MAXANGLE and MAXDIST have the same meaning as described above.

 10. If MPCTYPE = WLD is specified, the connection of the surfaces to the nodes in the
     corresponding sets is done according to the rules valid for the WLDSURFACE connection,
     see $MPC WLDSURFACE. It is done as follows:

        • The projection of nodes on the surfaces and element generation is done as de-
          scribed above in remark 8. The element type, however, must be SPRING6 in any
          case,




                                                                                                        Structure
        • NCPNT connection points of a circle with radius cradius around the projection point
          are coupled using a WLSCON connection, see $MPC WLSCON. The corresponding




                                                                                                          DAT
          finite elements in the domain are a part of the weld connection (see also remark 17).
        • Parameters MAXANGLE and MAXDIST have the same meaning as described above.

 11. If POSITION = FACE is used, the coordinates of the weld points are modified to the pro-
     jection points on the weld surface in any case. Note that model export contains the
     modified coordinates instead of the original coordinates for appropriate weld nodes.

 12. Depending on the type of spring element used, 3 or 6 degrees of freedom are used for
     dependent degrees of freedom definition for the MPCs, i.e. at the spring nodes.

 13. For beam elements, the connection points must not have identical coordinates, so only
     POSITION = FACE is allowed.

 14. The generated elements are assigned to a new element set with name name specified
     on header line. Element properties are assigned in the usual way in the system vari-
     ant, referring to that element set. For SPRING3, SPRING6 or beam-elements, the local
     element coordinate system is generated automatically where the local x′ -axis is parallel
     to the mean of the normals of the connected surface elements. The normal points from
     surf _1 towards surf _2 etc.. If surf _i and surf _(i+1) are at the same position, the direction
     of surf _i is used.

 15. The maximum allowable distance between the surfaces to be coupled must be specified
     by parameter MAXDIST in any case. Meaningful values depend on the geometry of the
     model and on the selected unit of length.

 16. To control neighborhood relation determination between points and surface elements,
     two parameters are available: DISTOL and OUTTOL. A point may be aligned to a surface
     element if its distance from the surface is less than DISTOL and its distance from the
     boundary of the element is less than OUTTOL. If not input, the default values defined
     by global system keys MPCDISTOL and MPCOUTTOL are used. For an explanation of
     MPCOUTTOL / MPCDISTOL parameter, refer to figure F3-2.

marks:

1. Definition of contacts is only possible in top or single components.

2. Label (integer, name or text string) of contact definitions must be unique within each
   constraint variant.

3. Contact names may be given as quoted text, too – e.g. to enclose mixed case or non-
   alphanumeric letters (note that ’MyName’ is different from ’MYNAME’, but the latter text
   is equal to the unquoted name token MYNAME).

4. For each contact definition the corresponding contact load properties have to be defined
   within the loading variant by a matching $CONTACT LOAD data line, see page 3-569.

5. If NODE is specified as 2nd partner (contact node to node, default), then each data
   line defines contacts between one or more pairs of nodes, which are referenced by the
   common contact definition label. The first list contains the first nodes of the contacts,
   the second list the second ones. First and second list must contain the same number of
   nodes. The same node must not appear in first and second list. Contact node pairs are
   formed by assigning to each node of one list that node from the other list with the smallest
   distance.

6. If LINENODE or SURFNODE is specified as 2nd partner (contact node to node of line/
   surface), then each data line defines contacts between all nodes of the 2nd partner
   line/surface and the nodes given as 1st contact partner.

7. If GROUND is specified as 2nd partner (contact node to ground), then each data line
   defines contacts between one or more nodes and ground, which are referenced by the
   common contact definition label. Only one list of nodes may be input. The contact coordi-
   nate system must be fixed with respect to a (possibly local) reference coordinate system
   (see remark 9).

8. At all contact nodes the degrees of freedom must be able to represent the contact normal
   direction. The degrees of freedom itself may be suppressed, prescribed or dependent.




82                    PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                        V 19.00.287
 10. Contact coordinate systems from $CONTACT NODE are always fixed for the entire con-
     tact analysis, they do not move or rotate with structural deformations.
 11. The contact coordinate system may be defined with respect to geometry, i.e. coordinates
     of first and second contact nodes, or with respect to a (possibly local) reference coordinate
     system. For contact node to ground a definition with respect to geometry is not possible.
 12. CONTSYS = DIRECT is intended to be used for geometry with (originally) open gap, i.e.
     with positive gap width δgeo . The xC -axis (contact normal direction) points from the first
     to the second contact node. The two nodes must not have identical coordinates. Only
     applicable for contacts node to node. Since yC - and zC -axes are fixed internally, optional




                                                                                                       Constraints
     friction must be isotropic.
 13. CONTSYS = INVERSE is intended to be used for geometry with (originally) overlapping




                                                                                                          DAT
     gap, i.e. with negative gap width δgeo . The xC -axis, with contact normal direction, starts at
     the first contact node. The two nodes must not have identical coordinates. Only applicable
     for contacts node to node. Since yC - and zC -axes are fixed internally, optional friction must
     be isotropic.
 14. A reference system may be given explicitly by CONTSYS = rsys, where CONTSYS = 0
     means component system. If the reference system is cylindrical or spherical, a local
     reference system is generated using the generation rules for rotated node bases, see
     page 1-11.
 15. If the contact coordinate system is fixed with respect to a (possibly local) reference sys-
     tem, two orthogonal directions defining xC - and yC -axes may be specified by selecting
     axis directions of the reference system via parameter AXES.
     If the AXES parameter is omitted, then AXES=X,Y is assumed. If only the normal direction
     idof n is specified (xC -axis), then the tangential direction idof y (yC -axis) is determined
     according to the following table:
                      idof n    i.e. xC -axis       −→ Default    i.e. yC -axis
                      given     is equivalent to     for idof y   is equivalent to
                     +X / +1    xr -axis               +Y / +2    yr -axis
                     +Y / +2    yr -axis                +Z / +3   zr -axis
                     +Z / +3    zr -axis               +X / +1    xr -axis
                     –X / –1    negative xr -axis       –Z / –3   negative zr -axis
                     –Y / –2    negative yr -axis       –X / –1   negative xr -axis
                     –Z / –3    negative zr -axis       –Y / –2   negative yr -axis

 16. If parameter FRICTION is omitted or FRICTION = NO is specified, friction is ignored for
     all contacts defined within current data block (default).
     If friction has to be taken into account and contact coordinate system is defined by geom-
     etry (CONTSYS = [ DIRECT / INVERSE ]), then only FRICTION = BOTH with isotropic
     friction should be used (since Y/Z direction is ambiguous).


V 19.00.287                    PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          3-283
ample:

! definition for individual node pairs
! normal direction from vector n1 -> n2
$CONTACT NODE CONTSYS=DIRECT
    101     1010 : 2010
    102     1010 : 2020
    103     1010 : 2030
    201     2010 : 3010

! definition by node sets
! normal direction (x_c) is negative x’-axis of ROTB system
! first friction direction (y_c) is y’, friction in z_c only
$CONTACT NODE CONTSYS=ROTB1 AXES=-X,Y FRICTION=Z
    CONTNAM1    NODESET_A : NODESET_B

! contact to ground, no friction
! normal direction is positive x-axis of component system
$CONTACT NODE CONTSYS=0 GROUND
    CONTNAM2    NODESET_G 1563 1567

! contact to ground, no friction
! normal direction is positive x-axis of RSYS 204
$CONTACT NODE GROUND CONTSYS=204
    CONTNAM12   1354673   1354674

88                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          V 19.00.287
  2. Label (integer, name or text string) of contact definitions must be unique within each
     constraint variant.

  3. Contact labels may be given as quoted text, too – e.g. to enclose mixed case or non-
     alphanumeric letters (note that ’MyName’ is different from ’MYNAME’, but the latter text
     is equal to the unquoted name token MYNAME).

  4. For each contact definition the corresponding contact load properties have to be defined
     within the loading variant by a matching $CONTACT LOAD data line, see page 3-569.

  5. If NODE is specified as 2nd partner (contact surface to node), then each data line defines
     contacts between the given nodes and their projection on the surface.




                                                                                                       Constraints
  6. If LINENODE or SURFNODE is specified as 2nd partner (contact surface to nodes of
     line/surface), then each data line defines contacts between all nodes of the 2nd partner




                                                                                                          DAT
     line/surface and their projection on the 1st partner surface, i.e. all nodes of the 2nd partner
     are contact nodes.

  7. Currently the LINE parameter is just an alias for LINENODE. However, in future releases,
     the behaviour of LINE may be extended to take into account backward-line contact, too.

  8. If SURFACE is specified as 2nd partner (contact surface to surface, default), then each
     data line defines contacts between each node of one surface with its projection on the
     other surface and vice versa, i.e. all nodes of both surfaces are contact nodes.

  9. If SELF is specified as 2nd partner (self contact) then each data line defines contacts
     between the nodes of a surface with all non-neighboring patches of the same surface
     (projection on the other parts of the same surface).

 10. If GROUND is specified as 2nd partner (contact surface to ground), then each data line
     defines contacts between each node of the surface and ground.

 11. If a list of surfaces or surface sets is specified, all surfaces are handled as one assembled
     surface to establish the contact points. Therefore, the specified surfaces must not overlap
     in order to avoid redundant contact pairs or ambigous contact neighborhood.

 12. At all contact nodes the degrees of freedom must be able to represent the contact normal
     direction. The degrees of freedom itself may be suppressed, prescribed or dependent.

 13. For each contact a contact coordinate system xC is established. For contact surface to
     surface and surface to node its origin is located at the position of the projection of the con-
     tact node on the opposite surface, i.e. if CONTSYS = NORMAL (default) is specified,
     then the xC -axis, along which the contact can open or close, is the normal on the surface
     and points towards (or opposite to) the contact node, and the yC - and zC -axes are fixing
     the tangential plane of the contact, whereas for CONTSYS = rsys the orientation of the
     contact system refers to the reference system rsys and axes idof n, idof y accordingly.
     For contact surface to ground the origin is located at the node itself.


V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           3-289
   numerical stability, especially if the surface node’s coordinate lack some precision and/or
   some DOFs of the contact nodes are constraint by a partial $MPC, $SUPPRESS or
   $PRESCRIBE. However, the drawback is that those contact normals stay fixed with re-
   spect to the reference system and will not be updated when using contact geometry
   update with CAGEOUP (see page 4-18ff. of [um550]).

5. If the contact coordinate system is fixed with respect to a (possibly local) reference sys-
   tem, two orthogonal directions defining xC - and yC -axes may be specified by selecting
   axis directions of the reference system via the AXES parameter.
   If the AXES parameter is omitted, then AXES=X,Y is assumed. If only the normal direction
   idof n is specified (xC -axis), then the tangential direction idof y (yC -axis) is determined
   according to the following table:

                   idof n    i.e. xC -axis       −→ Default    i.e. yC -axis
                   given     is equivalent to     for idof y   is equivalent to
                  +X / +1    xr -axis                +Y / +2   yr -axis
                  +Y / +2    yr -axis                +Z / +3   zr -axis
                  +Z / +3    zr -axis                +X / +1   xr -axis
                  –X / –1    negative xr -axis       –Z / –3   negative zr -axis
                  –Y / –2    negative yr -axis       –X / –1   negative xr -axis
                  –Z / –3    negative zr -axis       –Y / –2   negative yr -axis

   where index r means (local) reference system.

6. Contact coordinate systems from $CONTACT SURFACE are fixed for the entire contact
   analysis, i.e. they do not move or rotate with structural deformations, unless CONTSYS
   = NORMAL is used and CAGEOUP is not activated (=OFF).

7. If parameter FRICTION is omitted or FRICTION = NO is specified, friction forces are
   ignored for all contacts defined within current data block (default).

8. For axisymmetric models the contact definition may refer structural DOFs 1 & 2 only.
   Therefore FRICTION = BOTH is not possible for axisymmetric models (would lead to a
   contact pair with 3 DOFs).

9. If anisotropic friction is to be taken into account, and CONTSYS = NORMAL is spec-
   ified, then the yC -axis of the local contact coordinate system should be defined using
   parameter YREF, see F3-28 on page 3-294.

0. To control the neighborhood mapping between points and surfaces, two parameters are
   available: DISTOL and OUTTOL. A point is a possible contact partner if its distance in
   positive normal direction from the surface patches is less than distol (pf actor ∗ distol on
   the patch backside) and if its in-plane distance from the boundary of the surface is less
   than outtol. If not input, the default values defined by global system keys CADISTOL,

     Practical experience has shown that penetration factors less than 1.0 (e.g. setting switch




                                                                                                          DAT
     CADISPFACTOR respectively pf actor =0.1) are often reasonable assumptions since a
     lot of models have large open gaps (e.g. gear box teeth), but press-fit problems rarely
     use the same amount of overlap.
     Also note that - due to the discretization of element edges - sensible pf actor values
     should stay in range 0.01≤ pf actor ≤100.0 since more extreme values may lead to a
     strange neighborhood computation: E.g. partner points above an element face might get
     ignored, if the point in question lays below the ’smoothed’ contact surface (or vice versa).
     On the other hand there is no objective against setting pf actor =0.0 if the corresponding
     surface is perfectly flat.

 21. The parameter COMPLEMENT controls how many contact pairs will be created from the
     nodes of the first partner of a surface to surface contact (i.e. which node of the first part-
     ner is a ontact discretization point). If not input, the default value defined by global system
     key CASCOMPLEMENT is used (see page 2-32).
     The different settings are illustrated in figures F3-24-F3-26. The blue arrows mark the
     contact pairs at nodes from the second partner which are always used. The red arrows
     mark the contact pairs at the nodes from the first partner which are different for each
     setting. The default setting AUTO reduces the number of contact pairs compared to the
     setting ALL but takes into account all contact pairs which are important due to discretiza-
     tion and geometry differences, i.e. at the boundaries and at regions with a finer mesh on
     the first contact partner and with different normals on the contact partners, i.e. the angle
     between both normals is greater than CASCOMPANGLE (default value is 10◦ ). A contact
     pair at a node of the first contact partner is also taken into account if the normalized dis-
     tance to all nadir points in the adjacent patches is larger than the value of the UCI-switch
     CASURFMSR (see page 4-56ff. of [um550]).

Remarks:

  1. Contact regions may be locked according to the contact results of a referenced situation.
     The locking is done by an implicit generation of multipoint constraints on all contact nodes
     that match a corresponding locking condition:




                                                                                                       Constraints
        • For Node-To-Node or Surface-To-Node contacts the DOFs of the 2nd contact partner
          will be defined as dependents of the DOFs from the 1st contact partner.




                                                                                                          DAT
        • For Node-To-Ground or Surface-To-Ground contacts the DOFs of the 1st contact
          partner will be defined as suppressed or dependent according to their local ROTB
          system.
        • Surface-To-Surface coupling works perfectly well for contact analysis, but may cause
          cyclic MPC dependencies if both sides request mutual locks to opposing patches.
          Therefore Surface-To-Surface contacts are not recommended to be used together
          with contact locking, i.e. those contacts should be downgraded to a unique Surface-
          To-Node contact definition.

  2. The contact locking request is part of the component definition, and is valid for all situa-
     tions of this component.

  3. Contact labels cadef refer to $CONTACT definitions in the constraint variant of the refer-
     enced situation refsit in referenced component refcomp. Pretension label ptdef refer to
     $PRETENSION definitions with GUIDING=CONTACT in the structure block of the refer-
     enced component refcomp.

  4. Contact locking requests must be unique, e.g. for contact label cadef only one specifi-
     cation (only one data line) is possible. Moreover pretension labels must be unique with
     respect to contact label. In case a pretension label matches a contact label the pretension
     definition must be distinguished with a PRETEN_ prefix, e.g. PRETEN_MIX for preten-
     sion definition MIX (the PRETEN_ prefix can be used in any case, so it is good practice
     to use it even if both name spaces are separate).

  5. If the referenced component is not specified, then the current component is used.

  6. With the CASFILE option a consolidated contact situation together with a matching con-
     tact status file is sufficient as reference, i.e. at least a TASK STORE of e.g. STATIC [TO
     PRECHECK] is needed in the reference situation, but there is no need for an actual static
     analysis as the referred ’results’ are read from the given contact status file. The contact
     names/ids and nodal point IDs in the file must match the contact names/ids and nodes in



V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         3-297
   remark 14). Also in combination with FRICTION=MATRICES the user must ensure that
   the corresponding caso-file was written from a reference situation with $VELOSTATE and
   that no anisotropic friction is involved.

7. If contact locking is requested and no specific contact or pretension labels are specified
   at all, i.e. there is only one data block $CONTLOCK, and this data block contains only
   the first data line, then all contacts and pretensions (with GUIDING=CONTACT) of the
   referenced situation are taken into account. The same is true if there is a second data
   line but without contact label, only with parameter NORMAL and/or FRICTION.

8. If any contact is specified, then only the specified contacts are taken into account.

9. Coupling in the normal direction of contact is controlled by parameter NORMAL:
      • If NORMAL = FREE is specified, then the displacements in the normal direction
        are always uncoupled.
      • If NORMAL = LOCK_IF_ACTIVE (default) is specified, then the displacements in
        the normal direction are coupled if the contact is active.
      • For NORMAL = LOCK is specified, then the displacements in the normal direction
        are always coupled (independent of contact status).

0. Any NORMAL condition (apart from NORMAL=FREE) may be extended by an additional
   limit condition with a threshold value that must be matched before a corresponding LOCK
   is actually established, see remark 14 below.

1. In the tangential plane, coupling is possible only if the current dof type establishes at least
   3 DOFs per node (i.e. DOFTYPE=DISP) and if friction was taken into account by the
   referred $CONTACT definition. Then the coupling is controlled by parameter FRICTION:
      • If FRICTION = FREE (default) is specified, then the displacements in the tangen-
        tial plane are always uncoupled.
      • If FRICTION = LOCK_IF_ACTIVE is specified, then the displacements in the tan-
        gential plane are coupled if the contact is active (see ROTB restrictions below).
      • If FRICTION = LOCK_IF_STICK is specified, then the displacements in the tan-
        gential plane are coupled only if the contact is in stick (see ROTB restrictions below).
      • If FRICTION = LOCK is specified, then the displacements in the tangential plane
        are coupled in any case (independent of contact status, see restrictions below).
      • For FRICTION = MATRICES the displacements in the tangential plane are uncou-
        pled (like FRICTION=FREE), but will lead to additional damping matrices needed for
        some special dynamic analysis (e.g. brake-squeal analysis).

2. FRICTION = MATRICES is only allowed for DOFTYPE=DISP and in combination with
   NORMAL = LOCK_IF_ACTIVE (default).




98                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           V 19.00.287
 14. Each NORMAL and FRICTION parameter may be extended by one of the following limit
     conditions that must be hold before a corresponding LOCK is actually established:

                keyword        limit     range      coupling condition:
                MINPRESS       pN min    R          minimum normal contact pressure
                MINSHEAR       pF min    R ≥ 0.0    minimum fritcional shear
                MINFORCE       RN min    R          minimum normal contact force
                MINFRICF       RF min    R ≥ 0.0    minimum frictional force
                MAXGAP          δmax     R          maximum gap width
                MAXSLIP         δslip    R ≥ 0.0    maximum slip distance




                                                                                                      Constraints
     Options MAXGAP and MAXSLIP are not supported in combination with the CASFILE pa-
     rameter (see remark 6).




                                                                                                         DAT
     Also note that the frictional conditions (MINSHEAR, MINFRICF, MAXSLIP) may be used
     only if friction was taken into account and that limit values < 0.0 (for MINPRESS, MIN-
     FORCE, MAXGAP) are meaningfull only if the referred contact enforces active normal
     state by a corresponding LOCK, FIXED or FORCE parameter (see $CONTACT LOAD for
     details). Moreover, MAXGAP condition is usually only meaningfull together with NOR-
     MAL/FRICTION=LOCK.

 15. If a colon separated list of nodes is appended to the lock condition line then the given
     condition applies only to those contact nodes that are part of the extra list (instead of just
     all nodes of the corresponding contact definition). Node set names refer to the current
     component (nodal point identifiers as well as local ROTB systems of those nodes must
     match in current and reference component).


Example:

$CONTLOCK
   SITUATION=situ_0                                   ! from last result column of situ_0
   FRICTION=LOCK_IF_ACTIVE                            ! all contacts (& all pretensions)

$CONTLOCK
   SITUATION=situ_0
   CA1 NORMAl=LOCK,MAXGAP,0.1                            ! Lock CA1 if gap width <= 0.1
   CA2 FRICTION=LOCK_IF_ACTIVE,MINPRESS,100.0            ! Lock if active & CAPRESS>=100.0
   PreTen_BOLT NORMAL=LOCK                               ! Lock pretension BOLT

$CONTLOCK
   COMPONENT=orig SITUATION=situ_3           LPAT=200         ! from LPAT 200 of situ_3
   10001    NORMAL=LOCK_IF_ACTIVE                             ! for contact 10001
   cnt_456 FRICTION=LOCK_IF_STICK           : n_456_part      ! for nset n_456_part in

Remarks:

  1. Definition cyclic symmetry boundary conditions is only possible within a constraint variant
     of top or single components.

  2. Cyclic symmetry boundary conditions are available for real eigenvalue analysis, see
     VIBRATION ANalysis (see page 2-276 ff.), but only for SOLV = DIRECT, and for linear
     static analysis without contact, see STATIC (see page 2-267 ff.). In all other analyses the
     definition is ignored. Furthermore, variable partitioning is not allowed for cyclic symmetry
     analysis, therefore
            DEFAULT SET VPART=OFF
     must be included in the UCI-file before the NEW-command.

  3. A cyclic symmetric structure consists of N ≥ 2 identical sectors where each sector is
     rotated by sector angle ϕS = 2π/N with respect to the preceding sector about the axis of
     symmetry. Each sector is connnected to the following one in the same manner, and the
     last sector with first one in the same manner too.

  4. The axis of symmetry must coincide with the z ′ -axis of a cylindrical reference system
     given by system identifier rsys, see $RSYS (see page 3-240 ff.).


V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                              3-301
   the axis of symmetry must be collected in node set nsetl, and all nodes of the upper
   interface (to the following sector) with the exception of nodes on the axis of symmetry in
   node set nsetu. If existent, nodes on the axis of symmetry must be collected in node set
   nseta.

7. Lower and upper interfaces must have the same number of nodes, and for each node of
   the lower interface there must be a corresponding node at the upper interface where the
   position in space of both nodes differs only by a rotation with sector angle ϕS about the
   axis of symmetry.

8. All interface nodes (with the exception of nodes on the axis of symmetry), i.e. all nodes
   in sets nsetl and nsetu, must have rotated node bases which refer to the cylindrical ref-
   erence system rsys. The reference, however may be already resolved, i.e. rotated node
   bases may be given by points as long as the orientation matches the orientation derived
   from cylindrical reference system rsys.

9. External degrees of freedom must not be specified if there are cyclic symmetry boundary
   conditions.

0. All degrees of freedom at interface nodes (with the exception of nodes on the axis of
   symmetry) must be local, i.e. neither external nor prescribed, suppressed or dependent.

Remarks:

  1. Specification for MultiBlade Coordinate transformation for analysis of cyclic symmetric
     structures is only possible within a constraint variant of a subcomponent.

  2. The subcomponent must contain the complete cyclic symmetric structure.

  3. The cyclic symmetric structure must consist of N ≥ 3 identical sectors where each sector
     is rotated by sector angle ϕS = 2π/N with respect to the preceding sector about the axis
     of symmetry. Each sector is connnected to the following one in the same manner, and
     the last sector with first one in the same manner too.

  4. The idealization of the sectors must be identical, i.e. after rotation of sector i by ϕS its
     nodes must coincide with the corresponding nodes of sector i + 1. The same condition
     must be fulfilled for the degrees of freedom at those nodes.

  5. The axis of symmetry must coincide with the z ′ -axis of a cylindrical reference system
     given by system identifier rsys, see $RSYS (see page 3-240 ff.).

  6. At least one node must be located on the rotation axis, and all degrees of freedom at all
     nodes on the rotation axis must be declared as external if not suppressed or dependent.

  7. Degrees of freedom at nodes not on the rotation axis must not be external.

Multipoint constraint conditions can be defined in PERMAS within two different input brackets.
Definitions in the $STRUCTURE bracket are valid for all situations, whereas definitions in the
$CONSTRAINTS bracket are valid for specific situations only.
Multipoint constraint conditions must be defined for each degree of freedom type separately,
indicated by the DOFTYPE parameter. PERMAS automatically uses the multipoint constraints
corresponding to the degree of freedom type of the current analysis. Other definitions are
ignored.

marks:

1. Label (integer, name or text string) of MPC definitions must be unique within one compo-
   nent.

2. MPC labels may be also given as quoted text – e.g. to enclose mixed case or non-alpha-
   numeric letters (note that ’MyName’ is different from ’MYNAME’, but the latter text is equal
   to the unquoted name token MYNAME).

3. The dependent degrees of freedom will be introduced at the dependent nodes if not yet
   existent. For example, DPDOFS = 4 will create degree of freedom 4 at a node, even if
   (solid) elements connected to this node introduce only degrees of freedom 1, 2 and 3.

4. Dependent degrees of freedom form an own family of physical degrees of freedom, there-
   fore they cannot be declared as suppressed, prescribed or external. Of course a degree
   of freedom may appear only once as dependent degree of freedom, but can be used as
   guiding degree of freedom in other MPC conditions.

5. MPC conditions may be hierarchical, but not recursive.

6. The verification items MPC DEFinition, MPC GEOmetry and MPC SYStem can be
   requested by the user with the UCI-switch DEFAULT SET VERIFICATION.
   An export of internally resolved MPC definitions, e.g. one $MPC ISURFACE → multiple
   $MPC IQUAD4 definitions, is also available.

Neighborhood Detection
 Several MPC types use neighborhood search algorithms to identify corresponding guiding-
dependent partners. Of special interest is the $MPC ISURFACE definition, where different
search algorithms are available, depending on the parameter DPSYS.

   • If DPSYS = NORMAL is specified, then the same surface based neighborhood search
     as for contact definitions is used.

   • If DPSYS 6= NORMAL is specified, then a patch based neighborhood search by an
     OCTREE-method is used.

The neighborhood detection is controlled by the headerline parameters DISTOL and OUTTOL.
The default search tolerances can be modified by the UCI commands SET MPCDISTOL and
MPCOUTTOL. Figure F3-30 shows the meaning of the tolerance settings.

marks:

1. Please refer to the global MPC remarks which are valid for all MPC types.

2. If DPSYS = ROTB is specified, the coupling is done for the (possibly rotated) dependent
   degrees of freedom at nodes. Rotated node bases are taken into account automatically.

3. With DPSYS = rsys an explicit permanent local coupling coordinate system may be de-
   fined (rsys=0 for component system), i.e. its coupling directions are not influenced by any
   change of nodal point positions.

4. Together with DPSYS = rsys the AXES parameter may be used to specify two orthogo-
   nal directions defining xC - and yC -axes of the coupling coordinate system.
   If the AXES parameter is omitted, then AXES = 1,2 is assumed. If only the first direction
   idof x is specified (xC -axis), then the second direction idof y (yC -axis) is determined ac-
   cording to the following table:
                  idof x   first direction        −→ default     second direction
                  given    xC is equivalent to     for idof y    yC is equivalent to
                 +X / +1   xr -axis                  +Y / +2     yr -axis
                 +Y / +2   yr -axis                   +Z / +3    zr -axis
                 +Z / +3   zr -axis                  +X / +1     xr -axis
                 –X / –1   negative xr -axis          –Z / –3    negative zr -axis
                 –Y / –2   negative yr -axis          –X / –1    negative xr -axis
                 –Z / –3   negative zr -axis          –Y / –2    negative yr -axis

5. If DPSYS = MATRIX is specified, then the coupling system is specified explicitly by its
   base matrix.

6. If RELDOF is specified, then the additional degree of freedom identifier rdof is introduced
   for each dependent node controlling the relative movement between dependent and guid-
   ing nodes in principal direction. This is realized by an additional part urel of an extended
   constraint equation based on the first unit vector e1 of the local coupling system:

                            ud = Ag ug + urel ,      urel := urdof · e1 .




20                    PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                         V 19.00.287
  7. Application areas of MPC ILINE are butt joints of shell elements or coupling of line ele-
     ments.

  8. For all nodes with dependent degrees of freedom, interpolation relations are determined
     from guiding line or line set. The interpolation uses the normal projection of the dependent
     nodes onto the interpolation line.

  9. If a dependent node is not located on the guiding line, for translational degrees of free-
     dom the eccentricity of the node is taken into account by establishing a rigid lever arm
     connecting dependent node and projected point in order to preserve overall balance of
     external loads and reactions. The rigid lever arm correction requires a dependent DOF




                                                                                                    Constraints
     mask of 1,2,3,4,5,6, otherwise it will be omitted.




                                                                                                       DAT
 10. To control neighborhood relation determination between points and element lines, two pa-
     rameters are available: DISTOL and OUTTOL. A point may be aligned to an element line
     if its distance from the line is less than DISTOL ∗LE and its distance from the boundary of
     the element is less than OUTTOL ∗LE where LE is a typical element length. If not input,
     the default values defined by global system keys DISTOL and OUTTOL are used. See
     also general description on page 3-309.

 11. A table with statistical information on the neighborhood calculation of MPC ILINE connec-
     tions is printed in the result file.

 12. Rotated node bases are taken into account automatically. The interpolation is always
     true for the displacement components transformed into the (possibly rotated) bases at
     the nodes with dependent degree(s) of freedom.

   $MPC ILINE DPDOFS = 1,2,3 DPITYP = NODE DOFTYPE = DISP
     1000 201 : dep_nodes                     ! line id / node set

   $MPC    ILINE   DPDOFS = 1 DOFTYPE = PRES         DPITYP = NODE
     111   COUPL_LINE : NODE_SET_54                  ! line set / node set

6. If RELDOF is specified, then the additional degree of freedom identifier rdof is introduced

   ing nodes in principal direction. This is realized by an additional part urel of an extended

7. The coordinates of the guiding nodes define an isoparametrically curved quadrilateral
   surface as interpolation element. The interpolation uses the normal projection of the
   dependent nodes onto the interpolation surface. If dependent nodes are not located on
   the interpolation surface, for translational degrees of freedom node eccentricity is taken
   into account by establishing a rigid lever arm connecting dependent node and projected
   point in order to preserve overall balance of external loads and reactions.
8. If, for mechanical problems, the number of dependent dofs is chosen higher than the
   number of dofs at the guiding nodes, the kinematic motion of the guiding nodes (volume
   element(s)) is coupled with the dependent nodes (usually 6 degrees of freedom of the
   shell element node) in the following way:
      • The translational degrees of freedom are interpolated due to the shape function of
        the guiding region.
      • The rotational degrees of freedom of the dependent (shell) element nodes are inter-
        polated by the translations of the guiding region.

Remarks:

  1. Please refer to the global MPC remarks which are valid for all MPC types.

  2. If DPSYS = ROTB is specified, the coupling is done for the (possibly rotated) dependent
     degrees of freedom at nodes. Rotated node bases are taken into account automatically.

  3. With DPSYS = rsys an explicit permanent local coupling coordinate system may be de-
     fined (rsys=0 for component system), i.e. its coupling directions are not influenced by any
     change of nodal point positions.

  4. Together with DPSYS = rsys the AXES parameter may be used to specify two orthogo-
     nal directions defining xC - and yC -axes of the coupling coordinate system.
     If the AXES parameter is omitted, then AXES = 1,2 is assumed. If only the first direction
     idof x is specified (xC -axis), then the second direction idof y (yC -axis) is determined ac-
     cording to the following table:
                      idof x   first direction       −→ default    second direction
                      given    xC is equivalent to    for idof y   yC is equivalent to
                     +X / +1   xr -axis                  +Y / +2   yr -axis
                     +Y / +2   yr -axis                  +Z / +3   zr -axis
                     +Z / +3   zr -axis                  +X / +1   xr -axis
                     –X / –1   negative xr -axis         –Z / –3   negative zr -axis
                     –Y / –2   negative yr -axis         –X / –1   negative xr -axis
                     –Z / –3   negative zr -axis         –Y / –2   negative yr -axis



V 19.00.287                       PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                     3-337
   for each dependent node controlling the relative movement between dependent and guid-
   ing nodes in principal direction. This is realized by an additional part urel of an extended
   constraint equation based on the first unit vector e1 of the local coupling system:

                           ud = Ag ug + urel ,      urel := urdof · e1 .

   The degree of freedom identifier rdof may not be part of the activated degrees of freedom
   at the dependent node to prevent undesired movement constraints. Typically rdof = 9 of-
   fers a secure separation. The movement actuation urdof must be given by a $PRESCRIBE
   / $PREVAL definition for rdof of the dependent node.

7. For all nodes with dependent degrees of freedom, interpolation relations are determined
   from guiding surface or surface set. The interpolation uses the normal projection of the
   dependent nodes onto the interpolation (guiding) surface. If dependent nodes are not
   located on the interpolation surface, for translational degrees of freedom node eccentricity
   is taken into account by establishing a rigid lever arm connecting dependent node and
   projected point in order to preserve overall balance of external loads and reactions.

8. If, for mechanical problems, the number of dependent dofs is chosen higher than the
   number of dofs at the guiding nodes, the kinematic motion of the guiding nodes (volume
   element(s)) is coupled with the dependent nodes (usually 6 degrees of freedom of the
   shell element node) in the following way:

      • The translational degrees of freedom are interpolated due to the shape function of
        the guiding region.
      • The rotational degrees of freedom of the dependent (shell) element nodes are inter-
        polated by the translations of the guiding region.

   See also page 3-340.

9. To control neighborhood relation determination between points and element surfaces, two
   parameters are available: DISTOL and OUTTOL. A point may be aligned to an element
   surface if its distance from the surface is less than DISTOL and its distance from the
   boundary of the element is less than OUTTOL. If not input, the default values defined by
   global system keys MPCDISTOL and MPCOUTTOL are used. See also figure F3-30

0. A table with statistical information on the neighborhood calculation of MPC ISURFACE
   connections is printed in the result file.

1. For each node with dependent degrees of freedom a local coupling coordinate system
   xC is used to establish interpolation relations from guiding surface or surface set.
   If dependent nodes are not located on the interpolation surface, for translational degrees
   of freedom node eccentricity is taken into account by establishing a rigid lever arm con-
   necting dependent node and interpolation point in order to preserve overall balance of
   external loads and reactions.

      The coupling normal axis xC is derived from the surface normal nS at each dependent
      node’s nadir point N automatically (N is determined by the normal projection of the node
      onto the guiding surface geometry). ** By the variable plane > 0 a reference plane
      is selected from two of the three coordinate axes of the reference system rsys. For a
      cylindrical or spherical reference system the reference plane is built by a local cartesian
      system at the surface point according to the rules given on page 1-11. Parallel to this
      reference plane an intersection plane is established cutting the surface at the point in
      question, thus leading to a tangent line. The tangential vector ts is given by the vector
      product nR × nS . The yC axis of the local coupling coordinate system is then calculated
      by a rotation of ts about nS by angle γ. The third axis zC then completes this right-hand
      system.

                  +Y / +2    yr -axis                   +Z / +3    zr -axis
                  +Z / +3    zr -axis                   +X / +1    xr -axis
                  –X / –1    negative xr -axis          –Z / –3    negative zr -axis
                  –Y / –2    negative yr -axis          –X / –1    negative xr -axis
                  –Z / –3    negative zr -axis          –Y / –2    negative yr -axis

  5. If DPSYS = MATRIX is specified, then the coupling system is specified explicitly by its
     base matrix.

  6. If RELDOF is specified, then the additional degree of freedom identifier rdof is introduced
     for each dependent node controlling the relative movement between dependent and guid-
     ing nodes in principal direction. This is realized by an additional part urel of an extended
     constraint equation based on the first unit vector e1 of the local coupling system:

                              ud = Ag ug + urel ,      urel := urdof · e1 .




V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                          3-355
7. Each guiding node has always up to three potential degrees of freedom and the depen-
   dent degrees of freedom are constrained to the translational movement (or temperatures
   etc.) of the guiding node.
   Degrees of freedom at the guiding node which are not coupled to the structure have to be
   suppressed or prescribed.

8. If DPITYP = NODE is specified, then the constraint conditions are established between
   pairs of corresponding nodes. If the node sets are ordered, then node pairs are formed
   according to the sequence of nodes in the sets. If node sets are not ordered, then node
   pairs are formed by assigning to each node of the first set that node from the second
   set with the smallest distance. In any case, both sets must contain the same number of
   nodes.

9. If DPITYP = GROUND is specified, then homogeneous constraint conditions are estab-
   lished at the (dependent) nodes, i.e. declaring a prescribed/suppressed behavior which
   requires at least one unconstrained degree of freedom. Thus the definition of DPDOFS =
   1,2,3 is not supported.

0. If DPITYP = NODESAME is specified, then gid / gidset must consist of exactly one
   guiding node.

2. Rigid body movements are restricted to displacement degrees of freedom.

   describe any kinematic motion of the defined rigid region.

   to be guiding degrees of freedom, defining the rigid body movement entirely.

marks:

1. Please refer to the global MPC remarks which are valid for all MPC types.

2. If RELDOF is specified, then the additional degree of freedom identifier rdof is introduced
   for each dependent node controlling the relative movement between dependent and guid-
   ing nodes in principal direction. This is realized by an additional part urel of an extended
   constraint equation based on the initial position vectors xi :
                                                                   xd − xg
                        ud = Ag ug + urel ,     urel := urdof ·              .
                                                                  |xd − xg |

   The degree of freedom identifier rdof may not be part of the activated degrees of freedom
   at the dependent node to prevent undesired movement constraints. Typically rdof = 9 of-
   fers a secure separation. The movement actuation urdof must be given by a $PRESCRIBE
   / $PREVAL definition for rdof of the dependent node.

3. MPC RIGID is restricted to displacement or temperature degrees of freedom.

4. The node set for the guiding node must consist of only a single node.

5. If displacement degrees of freedom are constrained:

      • The guiding node has always six potential degrees of freedom, describing the possi-
        ble kinematic motion of a rigid region. Degrees of freedom at the guiding node which
        are not coupled to the structure have to be suppressed or prescribed.
      • Rotated node bases are taken into account automatically, i.e. the rigid body move-
        ment is transformed to the (possibly rotated) bases at the nodes with dependent
        degree(s) of freedom.

6. If temperature degrees of freedom are constrained:

      • The guiding node has always two potential degrees of freedom. Degrees of freedom
        at the guiding node which are not coupled to the structure (e.g. ∆T at solids) have
        to be suppressed or prescribed.
      • The constraints for T and ∆T are separated; there is no coupling between them.

Remarks:

  1. Please refer to the global MPC remarks which are valid for all MPC types.
  2. Weighted averaged connections are restricted to displacement or temperature degrees
     of freedom.
  3. The node set for the dependent node must consist of only a single node.




                                                                                                       Constraints
  4. If displacement degrees of freedom are constrained:
        • The sum of all guiding degrees of freedom must be capable to describe an arbitrary




                                                                                                          DAT
          kinematic motion of a rigid body, i.e. at the dependent point all six degrees of free-
          dom must be provisionally supported by the WLSCON – even if not all of them are
          taken as dependent DOFs !
        • The displacements at the guiding degrees of freedom are weighted by factor w and
          all guiding contributions are averaged by least square method to define the motion
          of a rigid body. The dependent degrees of freedom are constrained to that rigid body
          motion.
        • If gdof is omitted, all translational or all translational and rotational degrees of free-
          dom of the corresponding node gid are assumed to be guiding degrees of freedom.
          See also switch MPCWLSGDOF, SET/SHOW see page 2-41
        • Degrees of freedom at the guiding nodes which are not coupled to the structure have
          to be suppressed or prescribed.
        • It is not recommended to use rotational degrees of freedom as guiding degrees of
          freedom except if necessary regarding paragraph one (e.g. if the guiding nodes are
          collinear).
        • Rotated node bases are taken into account automatically, i.e. the displacements of
          the guiding nodes with (possibly rotated) local bases are transformed to the compo-
          nent system before calculating the rigid body movement.
  5. If temperature degrees of freedom are constrained:
        • If gdof is omitted, always two degrees of freedom of the corresponding node gid are
          assumed to be guiding degrees of freedom.
        • Degrees of freedom at the guiding nodes which are not coupled to the structure (e.g.
          ∆T at solids) have to be suppressed or prescribed.
        • The constraints for T and ∆T are separated; there is no coupling between them.
  6. If w is omitted, w = 1.0 is assumed.
  7. See also default switch WLSSCALE, DEFAULT see page 2-81

marks:

1. For specification of MPC names see remark 1 on page 3-126.

2. The definition of update rules for multipoint constraints is only possible within the con-
   straint variant of a single or top component.

3. For the update rules to be applied the update policy has to be set to MANUAL via the
   default switch (MPCUPDATE, DEFAULT see page 2-73). The MANUAL update includes
   an update of the constraints neighborhood relation if applicable like for e.g. for $MPC
   ISURFACE. In contrast, the automatic update does not update neighborhood relations.

4. The update of multipoint constraints is restricted to geometric nonlinear analyses, see
   NLMATERIAL and DIRECT NLTIME.

5. The update of multipoint constraints is only available for the following types:

      • RIGID, see $MPC RIGID,
      • WLSCON, see $MPC WLSCON,
      • RIGCON, see $MPC RIGCON and
      • WLSSURFACE, see $MPC WLSSURFACE.

   The update of interpolation region constraints of the types

      • ISURFACE, see $MPC ISURFACE,
      • ILINE, see $MPC ILINE and
      • IVOLUME, see $MPC IVOLUME

   is also available, but cannot be activated with parameter TYPE (also not with TYPE =
   ALL). The update of these types must be requested by a separate $MPCUPDATE without
   any TYPE specification and the label mpc in the data line.

6. Parameter NODES selects the nodes of the multipoint constraint definition to be updated.
   If NODES = GUIDING is specified, only the coordinates of the nodes with guiding de-
   grees of freedom are updated for the calculation of the modified constraint equations.


68                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                            V 19.00.287
  7. Only one update rule per multipoint constraint may be defined.

  8. If a node is affected by multiple constraints, then its coordinates must be updated either
     via all or none of these constraints.

Example:

  $MPCUPDATE
    15643 KIND = TRANS       NODES = ALL

marks:

1. If parameter RSYS or EULER is present on the $ROTB line, the indicated reference
   system is used to establish the rotated node bases. Reference systems are defined by
   data blocks $RSYS, see page 3-241ff. and figure F3-32 on following page. For cylindrical
   or spherical reference systems the local cartesian system for the orientation of the node
   basis is generated using the generation rules defined on page 1-11.
2. If Euler rotations are present then the given rotations are applied as consecutive intrinsic
   rotations to the axes of the rotated node basis derived from rsys in the sequence speci-
   fied (consecutive intrinsic rotations means that the 2nd / 3rd rotation is based on the new
   current axes derived from the 1st / 2nd rotation). Up to 3 rotations may be specified (same
   axis may be used for 1st and 3rd rotation).
3. If parameter RSYS and EULER are omitted, the local cartesian system for the orientation
   of the rotated node basis is established using three points according to rule valid to es-
   tablish a cartesian reference system, see page 1-11. Each point may be given by a node
   number or by its coordinates.
4. The coordinates of points may be given in the component system (default) or in any other
   reference system rsys, which may be a cartesian, cylindrical or spherical one.
5. Rotated node bases defined within the constraint variant bracket are valid only within
   current constraint variant. If rotated node bases should be the same for all constraint
   variants it is recommended to define them using the $ROTB data block within the structure
   definition bracket, see page 3-236.
6. If a nodal point carries external degrees of freedom, the rotated node basis must be
   defined in the structure definition bracket.
7. A rotated basis may not be defined for a hypercomponent node, which is defined via
   subcomponent coincidences (inserted via $SUBCOMP). The local system of this node
   must be defined in the subcomponent directly.

Remarks:

  1. Suppressed degrees of freedom form a separate degree of freedom family. They cannot
     be declared as prescribed or external nor be used as dependent degrees of freedom in
     MPC’s.

  2. For LINENODE or SURFNODE all nodes of the given lines / surfaces are suppressed,
     i.e. the constraint is applied to the nodes of the lines / surfaces not to the line / surface as
     such.

  3. The boundary condition is applied in the rotated basis system of the node. As an alter-
     native, $MPC NODE DPITYP = GROUND may be considered, which allows to apply a
     boundary condition independent of the rotated basis, but only for translational degrees of
     freedom.

     direct hypercomponent.

Remarks:

  1. Additional system matrices may be requested referring to another system variant by a
     $INSERT VARIANT data block.

  2. The additional system matrices depend on a constant load state of a foreign situation,
     which must be selected by a $ELSTATE LOAD data block. Constant load state and re-
     ferred system variant must belong to the same foreign situation.

  3. For linear STATIC and VIBration ANalysis, only additional symmetric stiffness matrices
     are considered.

  4. Following additional system matrices may be requested:
                      name              Matrix                Necessary load
                     GEOSTIFF         Geometric stiffness     Any load
                     CENTRISTIFF      Centrifugal stiffness   Constant rotation
                     PRESSTIFF        Pressure stiffness      Pressure loads
                     CORIOLIS         Coriolis matrix         Constant rotation
                     CONVSTIFF        Convective stiffness    Constant rotation
                     GYRO             Gyroscopic matrix       Constant rotation

     The necessary load given in the table for each matrix must be present in the constant
     load state, see $ELSTATE LOAD.



V 19.00.287                 PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                      3-393
7. For the dynamic analysis of rotating structures referring to the co-rotating frame of refer-
   ence, geometric stiffness, centrifugal stiffness and Coriolis matrix are needed. However,
   centrifugal stiffness as well as Coriolis matrix may be requested only if the geometric
   stiffness is included.

8. For the dynamic analysis of rotating structures referring to the inertial frame for reference,
   geometric stiffness, convective stiffness and gyroscopic matrix are needed. However,
   convective stiffness as well as gyroscopic matrix may be requested only if the geometric
   stiffness is included. Furthermore, the rotating part must be axisymmetric.

9. The pressure stiffness matrix (load correction matrix due to pressure loads) is available for
   all shell elements (only symmetric part until now) and for FSCPIPE2 elements. Pressure
   stiffness must not be requested without geometrical stiffness.

Remarks:

  1. Definition of static mode shapes to be added to the set of eigenvectors is possible only
     within a system variant of a single or top component (for an exception see remark 13),
     and is taken into account only in child situations for the transformation to modal space.
  2. Additional static mode shapes are available for analyses in modal space based on me-
     chanical (VIBRATION ANalysis (see page 2-276 ff.)), fluid (FLUID VIBration ANalysis (see
     page 2-144 ff.)) or coupled fluid-structure (FSCOUPLED VIBration ANalysis (see page
     2-147 ff.)) eigenvalue analysis.
  3. In coupled fluid-structure analyses, additional static mode shapes may be specified for
     displacement as well as for pressure degrees of freedom.
  4. If SOURCE = INPUT is specified, each data block defines one additional static mode
     shape. If SOURCE = LOAD or SOURCE = RESULT is specified, each data line defines
     one additional mode shape (for LPAT = ALL one for each load pattern). If SOURCE
     = ELEMENTS is specified, one additional mode shape per each natural deformation of
     each element is generated.




V 19.00.287                         PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                       3-397
      • In list(dof ) the nodal point degrees of freedom are specified; list(x) contains the
        corresponding nodal point values.
      • If list(dof ) is omitted then the sequence of nodal point values must correspond with
        the sequence of degrees of freedom, starting with 1. Trailing zeroes may be omitted.
      • Depending on dof type the nodal point values are displacements, pressures etc.
      • Shape values for rotational degrees of freedom are expected to be given in radians.
      • Input of shape values is not possible for degrees of freedom which are declared as
        suppressed, prescribed or external, or used as dependent degrees of freedom im
        MPC’s.
      • Input data may refer to a reference system given by parameter RSYS. If parameter
        RSYS is omitted, components of displacements etc. are referring to the (possi-
        bly rotated) local node coordinate system, RSYS = 0 means referring to component
        system. If the reference system rsys is a cylindrical or spherical one then input data
        refer to a local cartesian system which is generated according to the generation rules
        defined on page 1-11.

7. If SOURCE = LOAD is specified, additional mode shapes are calculated as static deflec-
   tions under the loads defined in the corresponding loading variant, one mode shape per
   specified load pattern. By LPAT = ALL all load patterns are specified. In any case, each
   load pattern may be specified only once.

8. If SOURCE = LOAD is specified in a collector situation where loading variants of different
   situations are assembled (see $SITUATION, parameter ASSEMBLY), then LPAT = ALL
   refers to all load patterns of all collected situations. If, however, LPAT = patid is specified,
   the load pattern patid must exist in all collected situations.

9. If SOURCE = RESULTS is specified, results of other situations are used as additional
   mode shapes. No result vector may be specified twice. If no selection is specified,
   COLUMN = LAST, i.e. last column of result book is assumed.

0. If SOURCE = ELEMENTS is specified, for each natural force (e.g. generalized force be-
   longing to elongation) of each specified element an additional static mode shape is gen-
   erated. This option, however, is restricted to spring, damper and control elements:

 11. If real eigenvalues are calculated with the MLDR-option (see UCI-command VIBRATION
     ANalysis (see page 2-276 ff.)), then the results must be transformed to origin component,
     i.e. the default CONF = ORIG must be used.

 12. If additional static mode shapes are requested in a modal coupled fluid-structure analy-
     sis, eigenvalue calculation without mass (by NOMASS = YES) or without compressibility
     (by NOCOMPR = YES) are not possible (see UCI command FSCOUPLED VIBration
     ANalysis (see page 2-147 ff.)). The same is true for approximation or neglecting singular
     coupling term by SCTAPP > 0.

 13. Additional static mode shapes by SOURCE = ELEMENTS may be requested in subcom-
     ponents. The degrees of freedom at the nodes of the corresponding elements, however,
     must be external ones in all components up to the top component if not suppressed.

 14. For mixed boundary static condensation the actual rigid body modes of the reference sit-
     uation are used to compute the inertia relief attachment modes. The modes must be
     requested in the reference situation used in the definition of $EXTERNAL MODEs. The
     modes are only available if the reference situation has rigid body modes.
     If requested in another analysis, the geometric rigid body modes for the free component
     are used to compute the load vectors for the inertia relief attachment modes.

 15. Modal damping by $MODDAMP may be specified for static mode shapes too (with the
     exception of modes defined by element deformations), but, however, the final sequence
     of modes is not known until the transformation to modal space is done.

                                                                        
                  ALPHA = α         BETA = β           G = gC0       , fun




                                                                                                   System
                                                                                                    DAT
 Item(s)            Type     Explanation
 α                 R≥0      Rayleigh coefficient α.
 β                 R≥0      Rayleigh coefficient β.
 gC0               R≥0      Structural damping reference value.
 fun               I>0      Label (integer, name or text string) of structural damping function.
                  name/text


Remarks:

  1. Overall damping may be defined for any top, single or subcomponent. In addition, it may
     also be specified in system variants of child situations where data from another system
     variant are inserted, see $INSERT VARIANT.

  2. Overall damping may be used for any kind of dynamic analysis where damping may be
     applied (including fluid-structure-coupled analysis) but not for modal spectral response
     analysis, see MODAL SPECTRAL ANalysis (see page 2-234 ff.).

  3. If overall damping is defined in a subcomponent, the complete reduced stiffness or mass
     matrix is taken into account, i.e. Guyan as well as Craig-Bampton parts. Furthermore, no
     component above in the configuration may contain the same type of overall damping.

  4. If overall damping is defined in a single or top component, then the corresponding damp-
     ing matrix in modal space is diagonal.

  5. Rayleigh (proportional) damping leads to the viscous damping matrix

                                           D = αK + βM




V 19.00.287                   PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                        3-401
6. Overall structural damping yields a complex stiffness matrix of the form

                                     K̄ = (1 + igC (f ))K

   with damping factor
                                     gC (f ) = gC0 fun g (f )
   which may be frequency-dependent in top or single components only. For transient re-
   sponse analysis, overall structural damping is converted to equivalent viscous damping
   by
                                              gC (fC )
                                       Dg,C =          K
                                               2πfC
   The reference frequency fC must be defined within the same system variant by parameter
   RFREQC, see data block $PARAMETER.

7. For single or top components, structural damping function can be defined as a general
   frequency-dependent function, see $FUNCTION. If the function identifier is omitted, the
   function is replaced by the constant value 1.0 .

ample:

$COMPDAMP
  ALPHA = 0.02     BETA = 0.05          ! Rayleigh damping

$COMPDAMP
  G = 0.04,101                    ! frequency dependent structural damping

Remarks:

  1. Initial values and admissible discrete values for design variables may be defined only in
     system variants of single or top components.

  2. Initial values of design variables must be greater than zero, except for design variables
     used for coordinate modifications, by $DSVNODE and $DVCOOR, if an OPTIM command
     is executed.

  3. Initial values are ignored for design variables, which are dependent due to design variable
     linking.

  4. If design variables are specified as basic variables by $BASVAR, initial values are defined
     by mean values (expectation) of the corresponding probability distribution functions, and
     must not be input directly.

  5. If for an geometrical property design variable no initial value is defined, then the initial
     value for optimization is calculated from original properties and property to design variable
     relation. This is, however, only possible for direct relations and must be without any
     contradiction, see page 3-410 for further details.

  see page 3-1149. Selection of discrete values is not possible for topological optimization.

marks:

1. Design variable to design node coordinate relations may be defined only in system vari-
   ants of single or top components.

2. The direction of coordinate modification is specified by the coordinate identifier idcoor,
   which may refer to component system (default), a reference system rsys (see remark 3)
   or to a surface surf (see remark 4).

3. If the reference system rsys is a cylindrical or spherical one, then the coordinates refer to
   a local cartesian system which is generated according to the generation rules defined on
   page 1-11.
4. If the coordinate refers to a surface, the design node must belong to the surface. The
   x-axis matches the surface normal at the design node as specified in the $SURFACE
   definition. Only for nodes on the surface boundary additionally y- and z-axes are available.
   These directions are coplanar to the surface tangent plane and approximate the normal
   and tangent to the boundary, see figure F3-33.

                         node on surface     node on surface boundary




                         x                                  x

                                                                    z



                                                                y



                       Figure F3-33: Coordinates for surface nodes


5. For any combination of nodal point, coordinate direction and design variable only one
   relation may be defined.

                                                             (i)         (0)

 10. If no initial values is defined for a design variables used for shape optimization it takes the
     default value zero.

 11. There are some implications arising from coordinate update during shape optimization:

        • Reference systems and surface normals are not updated even if nodal points used
          for their definition are moved.
        • If element systems are defined explicitly, their orientation in space is retained with
          the exception of beam elements where the orientation may be changed.
        • Anisotropic material and material systems are not supported in shape optimization.
        • If element nodes must coincide (e.g. SPRING3), each node must have the same
          coordinate dependency (not tested until now).

Remarks:

  1. Design variable to geometrical data relations may be defined only in system variants of
     single or top components.




                                                                                                            System
  2. All design variables dsvid referenced within one Geometrical Data Record must be as-
     signed to the same design element deid. The defined relations are then valid for all ele-




                                                                                                             DAT
     ments with the specified Geometrical Data Record and assigned to that particular design
     element. Elements with different Geometrical Data Records or elements not assigned to
     that design element are not concerned.
  3. Geometrical Data Records contain named parts called fields, see $GEODAT data block
     description, where each field contains a list of geometrical data. Within a field f ield,
     one particular item can be identified by its index. Consequently, the dependency of geo-
     metrical data on design variables is inputted referring to field name f ield and index ind.
     Repeated fields may be distinguished using the field repetition counter rep.
  4. For direct dependencies there is only one design variable per data line, for functional
     dependencies one tuple with n items where n is the number of independent variables
     of the corresponding function. All design variables must be valid for the whole design
     element.
  5. To relate design variables and properties, the following reference values X are used:
          • If a design variable is valid for the whole design element then the reference value X
            is given by the design variable value itself
  6. If KIND = DIRECT is specified, a linear relationship exists between reference value Xj
     and property value Pj , defined by
                                                                             (0)
                                 (i)                                      Pj
                                Pj     = Cj X (i) (ξj )   with   Cj =

               (i)
       where Pj      is the property j at the i-th iteration, X (i) (ξ j ) is the corresponding reference
                                                                 (0)
       value at point ξ j , and Cj is the original property Pj divided by the original reference
       value X (0) (ξ j ).
       Initial values of the corresponding design variables may be calculated as mean values of
       the related properties, see remark 9.
       In any case, for KIND = DIRECT the property value used for the first optimization step is
       always the original value.

   property value for the first optimization step is calculated according to the given function
   without reference to the original property value.

8. If NODES = ALL is specified, all properties referred within current data block get the
   same dependency at all element nodes. Option NODES = ALL is available for all Geo-
   metrical Data Record types where it is available for property input by data blocks $GEODAT.
   Nevertheless, specification of NODES = ALL for data blocks $DVGPAR and $GEODAT
   may be done completely independent.

9. Initial values of the design variables may be calculated if KIND = DIRECT is specified.
   The initial value is then calculated as the mean value of all property values of all Geomet-
   rical Data Records which are dependent on that design variable.

  3. A material property datum is referenced by the material property name prname (e.g.

     dependencies must be specified by paramater DEP on the header line, and the sequence
     of dependency specification determines the sequence of independent variables (state
     variables) of the function c(y).

marks:

1. Design variable to system parameter relations may be defined only in system variants of
   single or top components.

2. A design variable to system parameter relation may be restricted to a region, set etc. by
   specifying the corresponding identifier or name.

3. If KIND = DIRECT is specified, a linear relationship exists between design variable x and
   the value P of the parameter in question. So it holds

                                                                P (0)
                                   P (i) = C x(i)   with   C=
                                                                x(0)

     If P (0) = 0, the initial value of the design variable x(0) must be equal zero and vice versa,
     leading to C = 1.0.
     In any case, for KIND = DIRECT the parameter value used for the first optimization step
     is always the original value P (0) = 0.

4. If KIND = FUNCTION is specified, a functional dependency exists between value P of
   the parameter in question and m design variables xj , and so it holds
                                                    (i)
                                      P (i) = fun(xj , j = 1, m)

     For function definition see $FUNCTION data block description, pages 3-1112 ff..
     Initial values of the corresponding design variables cannot be calculated for general func-
     tion dependency but must be defined within a $DSVVAL data block. Furthermore, the
     parameter value for the first optimization step is calculated according to the given func-
     tion without reference to the original parameter value.

5. Initial values of the design variables may be calculated if KIND = DIRECT is specified.
   The initial value is then calculated as the mean value of all system parameters dependent
   on that design variable. For details see below.

     where the function argument is the filling ratio of the correspondig element.
     If the referred property field has data for multiple nodes or if the field is repeated, the
     relation is established for all data. This equals the NODES = ALL option in $DVGPAR.
  6. If KIND = PLY is specified, the original ply material data (ply thickness t0 or angle a0 ,
     see $PLY) are modified by the filling ratios.

     Ply thickness (ind = 1 in the data line) is modified by the relation
                                                        x
                                              t(x) = t0
                                                        x0
     Hence if the initial value for the filling ratios x0 equals the initial ply thickness t0 , the
     modified thicknesses also equal the actual filling ratio values. If a function is specified in
     the data line the relation changes to
                                                        f (x)
                                            t(x) = t0
                                                        f (x0 )


     Ply angles (ind = 2 in the data line) are modified by the relation
                                         a(x) = a0 + x − x0


V 19.00.287                  PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)                           3-421
7. If FILL = FIXED is specified, the filling ratio of all elements assigned to the design ele-
   ment is kept constant during the optimization process, but volume and mass is taken into
   account when computing the volume / mass reduction of the optimized structure.

ample:

ase refer to examples of topology optimization starting with example TOPO1 of [um550].

$DVTPAR DEID = 1001                                 ! KIND = SQUARE

$DVTPAR DEID = 1002      KIND = POWER    FILL=VAR ! power approach with exponent 3.0
  3.0

   KEEP, however, the element distribution at the boundaries of that set is kept. If BOUND-
   ARY = KEEP is specified for all element regions, i.e. for all element sets included in the
   coarsening process, a compatibly coarsened mesh is achieved in any case.
